title: Ocean Mining Rejects Complicity Claims Over Luxor Bitcoin Pool Hack
summary: Bitcoin mining pool operator Ocean Mining has denied involvement in a cyberattack targeting Luxor’s Commander software, insisting that its systems were never compromised. It added that payments associated with the incident were processed under its permissionless, noncustodial reward distribution mod...
content:
Bitcoin mining pool operator Ocean Mining has denied involvement in a cyberattack targeting Luxor’s Commander software, insisting that its systems were never compromised. It added that payments associated with the incident were processed under its permissionless, noncustodial reward distribution model.

Key Takeaways

  • Ocean Mining says its systems were unaffected by the Luxor hack, disputing Luke Dashjr’s allegation.
  • Ocean defends Bitcoin’s permissionless payouts despite claims attackers received over $10,000 in rewards.
  • Ocean pledges to cooperate with Luxor and law enforcement as questions persist over 0.33 BTC in future payouts

Ocean Defends Permissionless Mining

In a statement posted on X, Ocean acknowledged that the security breach resulted in the unauthorized redirection of mining computing power, or hashrate, belonging to Luxor and its customers to other mining pools, including Ocean.

However, the company maintained that its infrastructure operated normally throughout the incident and rejected any suggestion that it participated in the attack.

“Ocean was not compromised. Our systems operated normally. We had no involvement in the incident,” the company said.

The statement follows accusations by Bitcoin developer and former Ocean chairman Luke Dashjr, who alleged that the mining pool knowingly facilitated payments to the attackers and collected fees from mining activity linked to the breach.

Ocean did not directly name Dashjr or address the specific figures he cited. Instead, its response focused on the principles governing its payout system, arguing that blocking or redirecting rewards for valid mining work would undermine Bitcoin’s permissionless nature.

“Bitcoin is either permissionless or it is not. There is no middle ground,” Ocean declared.

Ocean Says Valid Mining Work Cannot Be Reassigned

At the center of Ocean’s defense is its TIDES payout system, which the company says automatically accounts for valid proof of work and distributes mining rewards directly to participants without requiring them to surrender custody of their funds. According to Ocean, the system verifies the validity of submitted mining work but does not determine whether the submitting party owns the mining equipment or was authorized to configure it.

“We verify the work submitted, but not who owns the machines or whether someone was authorized to configure them,” Ocean explained.

The company added that once valid work has been submitted, the corresponding credit cannot be reassigned under its payout rules. Although the mining activity may have originated from equipment redirected without its owners’ consent, Ocean argues that its system is designed to process valid work according to predetermined rules rather than make discretionary judgments about who should receive the associated rewards.

Ocean further argued that allowing a mining pool to selectively block or redirect payouts would introduce centralized control over miners’ earnings.

“Permissionless mining isn’t a loophole. It’s a principle,” the company said.

It added that a pool capable of arbitrarily deciding whose valid work counts, who receives payment, or when established rules apply would require miners to trust the operator with powers Bitcoin was designed to eliminate.

Dashjr Alleged Ocean Profited From Attack

Ocean’s explanation comes after Dashjr accused the company of financially benefiting from the hijacking of Luxor customers’ mining operations. In his post, Dashjr claimed that Ocean had instructed participating miners to direct 0.16202083 BTC, valued at approximately $10,510 at the time, to the attackers in two instances after the incident became public.

He further alleged that the pool was continuing to allocate rewards equivalent to 0.08123485 BTC, or approximately $5,270, to the attackers and that its website indicated plans for another 0.33029017 BTC, worth roughly $21,400, in subsequent distributions.

Dashjr also claimed Ocean had already collected 0.00330655 BTC, valued at approximately $210, in fees associated with the compromised mining activity and stood to receive another 0.0066058034 BTC, or approximately $440. Together, the amounts would total nearly 0.01 BTC, worth approximately $650 at the prices cited by Dashjr.

“Yes, that’s right: Ocean is profiting from a cyberattack on their own customers, and rewarding the attackers,” Dashjr wrote.

Ocean Points to Risks of Centralized Mining Infrastructure

Beyond defending its payout mechanism, Ocean used the incident to highlight what it described as the risks of centralized mining infrastructure.

According to the company, the unauthorized redirection of Luxor’s hashrate demonstrates the vulnerabilities miners face when they delegate operational control of their equipment to third-party software providers.

“This incident underscores a fundamental risk of centralized mining: When you entrust control to a third party, you also inherit the risks of that third party’s systems,” Ocean said.

Ocean also expressed sympathy for affected miners and pledged to cooperate with Luxor, law enforcement, and customers investigating the attack. The company urged miners to secure access to their equipment, update security measures, and monitor their mining configurations for unauthorized changes.

title: CoW Swap Adds Native Solana Trading With Solver Auctions and a One-Year Volume-Fee Waiver
summary: CoW Swap has launched an alpha that allows traders to start and finish asset swaps on Solana, extending an intent-based model previously associated with Ethereum. The.
content:
TL;DR

  • CoW Swap has opened a native Solana alpha using intent-based orders and competitive solvers.
  • Kamino is integrating the new service, according to launch reporting.
  • CoW DAO is waiving its volume fee for at least a year, not every possible trading cost.

CoW Swap has launched an alpha that allows traders to start and finish asset swaps on Solana, extending an intent-based model previously associated with Ethereum. The basic difference is worth understanding: rather than manually choosing a route and submitting a conventional swap, users sign an instruction that competing solvers try to execute at acceptable terms. CoW DAO is also waiving its own volume fee on Solana for at least a year, a decision that should not be mistaken for the disappearance of all trading costs.

Native Solana execution changes the product

Before this release, CoW Swap could facilitate certain routes into Solana from Ethereum-compatible networks. The new alpha supports trades whose starting and ending assets are on Solana itself. That is a different proposition for applications already serving Solana users. The launch includes an integration with lending platform Kamino and access to a solver network that CoW DAO describes as comprising more than 30 participants. The alpha designation also matters: traders should check supported assets, order conditions and current operational limitations before assuming every feature available on other chains is identical.

An intent describes the result, not every step

With an intent-based order, a trader specifies the assets and the price or conditions they will accept. Solvers can compete to find a matching trade or route liquidity through available venues. CoW Swap says its batching and execution design can help reduce opportunities for certain sandwich attacks and avoid some failed on-chain swaps. That is a design objective, not a guarantee that every order will fill at the best imaginable price. Market depth, slippage, solver incentives and latency still shape outcomes, especially for thinly traded tokens.

For related context, see our earlier report on Solana confidentiality infrastructure.

What the volume-fee waiver covers

CoW DAO says it will waive its own Solana volume fee for at least the first 12 months. Users should distinguish that platform charge from the economic costs of crossing bid-ask spreads, securing liquidity and potentially using network resources. Sponsored transactions can also change who pays an upfront network fee without making trade execution economically costless. The order’s displayed execution price and the eventual tokens received remain the meaningful comparison with other venues. Fee promotions are useful, but not a substitute for checking route quality.

Why this matters for DEX competition

Solana already has active trading infrastructure, so the question is not whether CoW Swap brings decentralized exchanges to a previously empty market. It is whether solver competition and order batching create a sufficiently different experience to attract liquidity and integrations. For lending applications, a reliable swap path can also affect liquidation and portfolio-management workflows. Independent measurements of fills, failed attempts, spreads and protection against adverse ordering will be more persuasive than the cumulative trade-volume figures of the protocol’s older networks.

Execution quality needs independent measurement. Users comparing an intent-based solver with a traditional aggregator should examine the final amount received after all network and protocol costs, the time needed to settle and how failed or partially filled routes are handled. The headline fee waiver should not obscure transaction costs or liquidity-provider economics that may still apply. Solana's faster settlement can improve the experience, but it does not by itself guarantee that every swap will beat a direct exchange quote under volatile market conditions.

For related context, see our earlier report on a recent DeFi market-security case.

The launch adds another execution model to Solana, not a guarantee against losses or manipulation. Users should treat an alpha product’s safeguards and fee arrangements as claims to verify through its documentation and trading results as adoption grows.

Reporting sources: The Block report with CoW DAO announcement details

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Maple Finance CEO targets up to $15B in assets by the end of 2027
summary: Sidney Powell aims to reach $15 billion in assets under management by the end of 2027 as the firm looks to expand into tokenized lending and traditional finance.
content:
Onchain asset manager Maple Finance is aiming to grow its assets under management (AUM) to between $10 billion and $15 billion by the end of 2027 as it looks to attract more traditional financial (TradFi) firms, according to CEO Sidney Powell.

In an exclusive interview with Cointelegraph on Monday, Powell said the company is also targeting a loan book of around $4.5 billion to $5 billion.

The plans come as Maple looks to grow beyond lending backed primarily by cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin (BTC) and attract more traditional financial firms, with Powell expecting tokenized assets and stablecoins to play a major role in the company’s growth.

Maple reported $4.7 billion in AUM at the end of the third quarter, up 18% from a year earlier. However, Maple’s dashboard showed around $3.9 billion in AUM on Tuesday.

Outstanding loans rose 12% from a year earlier to $1.7 billion, while quarterly revenue increased 5% to $4.4 million, bringing annualized revenue to $17.6 million. Still, outstanding loans fell 9% from the previous quarter, while quarterly revenue remained flat.

Tokenized assets are digital versions of traditional assets, such as stocks and bonds, that can be held and traded on a blockchain. Separately, stablecoins are digital tokens designed to maintain a stable value relative to a reference asset, most commonly a currency such as the US dollar.

The market for tokenized real-world assets has grown significantly over the past year, with their value on public blockchains reaching about $39.9 billion as of Nov. 11, up 52% year-over-year, according to RWA.xyz. The value of tokenized stocks alone rose from about $678 million in January to nearly $3.9 billion in November.

Maple assets under management. Source: Maple Finance

Maple looks to TradFi for its next stage of growth

Powell expects tokenized stocks to grow fivefold to tenfold in 2027, which could allow Maple to offer loans backed by tokenized shares rather than relying mainly on cryptocurrency collateral.

“I think tokenized equities are going to be really big,” he said. “You’ll start to see more tokenized equity lending.”

Under this model, borrowers could use tokenized stocks as collateral to obtain loans without having to sell their investments, similar to how Bitcoin-backed lending works today.

“Ultimately, that’s really positive for the space because it gives you tokenized assets to lend against that are not correlated with Bitcoin,” Powell said. Bitcoin is the largest cryptocurrency with a market capitalization of over $1.28 trillion as of Nov. 17.

Maple is also discussing credit facilities through which banks would finance its Bitcoin-backed lending, Powell said.

“At the moment, we’re looking at a first deal where we’re speaking with banks about warehouse facilities for the Bitcoin-backed lending, so they would be a funder to us,” Powell said.

Maple already provides financing for a warehouse facility supporting Kraken’s crypto-backed lending program, which was announced in June. The proposed bank arrangements would instead bring funding into Maple’s lending business.

Powell added that Maple could pursue separate deals with US banks and lenders involving loans originated by TradFi institutions and subsequently brought onto blockchain networks. “I think that’s going to be a big market for 2027,” he said.

Maple outlined plans in September to lend against portfolios of asset-backed and mortgage-backed securities and finance loans originated by fintech companies. It said at the time that each new strategy would initially be capped at 5% of its overall deposit base.

Another priority is expanding partnerships with financial technology companies and digital banks that want to offer customers ways to earn interest on their stablecoin holdings. Powell said Maple is already in discussions with several large firms about potential products, with announcements possible in the first quarter of 2027.

“My view is that’s the kind of path Maple has to go down in order to grow, and we have to focus more on these larger institutional allocators,” Powell said. “That’s ultimately where most of the balance sheet is in traditional finance.”

That approach to expansion is also at the center of a leadership disagreement, according to Powell.

Related: Arch Lending eyes tokenized stocks as next collateral market

Leadership shakeup comes amid expansion plans

Maple’s growth plans come amid a leadership shakeup after co-founder and executive chairman Joe Flanagan and chief operating officer Ryan O’Shea announced plans last week to leave over disagreements about the company’s future direction.

Flanagan said his differences with Powell involved strategy and leadership, while O’Shea said he had reached a different view on the direction Maple should take.

Powell said the differences centered on how best to expand the business, particularly as TradFi institutions become more involved in crypto lending.

“We had a difference of opinion on the best way to scale things,” he told Cointelegraph. “This year, I think, more than ever, we started to see that real convergence with traditional finance, fintechs and neobanks. And my view is that that is kind of the right path for us to scale.”

The planned departures prompted questions from Maple’s investors, partners and clients, some of whom contacted Powell seeking clarification. Powell said the departures were unrelated to problems with Maple’s loan book or the health of the business.

“The important thing is conveying to them and reassuring them that this wasn’t to do with any issues in Maple’s loan book or any issues with the business,” Powell said. “It is just a difference on what is the best pathway to scale Maple from here.”

Maple Finance’s native token, SYRUP is currently trading at $0.103 as of 6:50 pm UTC on Tuesday, with a market capitalization of $123 million, according to CoinMarketCap. The token is down about 46% over the past 30 days and 74% over the past year.

title: Arthur Hayes Expects These 4 Coins to Pump Before the AI Bubble Pops
summary: Four cryptocurrencies could rally before the AI bubble ends, Arthur Hayes predicted. His outlook paired the prospect of gains with limited conviction, as an approaching stock market debut complicated the picture for crypto. 4 Tokens Form Hayes’ ‘Four Horsemen’ Arthur Hayes, co-founder of cryptocurre...
content:
Four cryptocurrencies could rally before the AI bubble ends, Arthur Hayes predicted. His outlook paired the prospect of gains with limited conviction, as an approaching stock market debut complicated the picture for crypto.

Key Takeaways

  • Hayes named ether, zcash, near, and venice in his rally forecast.
  • His listed levels were $2,800, $1,800, $6, and $40, respectively.
  • Small-to-medium positions accompanied his warning about an AI bubble.

4 Tokens Form Hayes’ ‘Four Horsemen’

Arthur Hayes, co-founder of cryptocurrency derivatives exchange Bitmex and chief investment officer at crypto investment firm Maelstrom, named ether, zcash, near, and Venice’s VVV in a bullish outlook on X on Nov. 16. His four-token outlook anticipated rising prices before the end of the AI bubble. The forecast paired that expectation with limited conviction and restrained position sizes.

Describing his selections, Hayes stated:

“The Four Horsemen shall pump and then usher in the end of the AI bubble:”

He listed ether (ETH) at $2,800, zcash (ZEC) at $1,800, near (NEAR) at $6.00, and AI platform Venice’s token (VVV) at $40. Venice operates an AI platform, with its token linked to access to computing capacity. As of this writing, ETH traded at approximately $1,794, ZEC at $921, NEAR at $3.24, and VVV at $20.25.

Hayes limited his trading exposure to small-to-medium positions, citing modest conviction. “The size is small to medium as conviction is meh, but if the music playing you gotta dance,” he clarified.

The comments followed his increased crypto exposure ahead of Anthropic’s IPO. On Nov. 11, Hayes said he was adding crypto risk before the anticipated initial public offering of AI giant Anthropic, the company behind Claude. He kept those positions small to medium so he could close them quickly, making flexibility part of his approach before identifying the four assets.

Crypto Fear Persists as Ether Buying Continues

That trading stance emerged against weak market sentiment. The Fear and Greed Index registered “extreme fear” at 10 on Nov. 16, compared with 29 a week earlier and 55 a month proor. Cryptoquant contributor Darkfost highlighted the reading alongside a 30-day average of 28.2, showing sharper pessimism in the daily measure than the monthly trend.

Institutional ether buying continued during the downturn, with treasury company Bitmine Immersion Technologies (NYSE: BMNR) disclosing holdings of approximately 6.08 million ETH on Nov. 16. Its latest acquisition added 7,653 ETH to that balance. Chairman Tom Lee suggested investors preparing for Anthropic’s IPO could be contributing to ether’s selling pressure, connecting his assessment of market weakness to the listing Hayes had anticipated.

Vaneck Head of Digital Assets Research Matthew Sigel argued on Nov. 16 that Anthropic’s IPO could divert capital from bitcoin. Comparing the setup with SpaceX’s listing, he suggested bitcoin’s near-term low could arrive in early December. His projection depended on that historical pattern repeating, offering a more cautious assessment of crypto’s immediate prospects around the AI listing.

NEAR Proposal Awaits Validator Adoption

A separate development affected another of the selected assets. NEAR disclosed the ratification of a proposed issuance reduction on Nov. 16 after the Security Council’s review window closed without a veto. The proposal would gradually lower maximum annual issuance from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months, slowing dilution while reducing newly issued staking rewards.

Validator adoption through a protocol upgrade remained necessary for the change to become binding. The planned sequence included a full-quarter grace period after ratification, with the gradual reduction scheduled to begin at the end of that quarter. The proposal modeled 11.8 million fewer NEAR tokens issued over two years compared with maintaining the 2.5% cap.

title: Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100
Bitcoin price slipped near $64,000 Tuesday afternoon as Strategy (MSTR) shares fell below the company's STRC preferred and Coinbase and other crypto stocks declined.
This post Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as...
content:
Bitcoin price slipped near $64,000 on Tuesday afternoon, as Strategy (MSTR) and Coinbase (COIN) shares fell and traders waited on Nvidia’s first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. The bitcoin price had climbed back to about $65,000 before the U.S. open, after holding near that level on Monday. Selling picked up once stocks turned lower, and bitcoin price slipped to about $63,300 at its low.

Strategy and Coinbase shares slide

Strategy shares were recently down more than 5% to about $97, dropping below $100 and trading under the company’s STRC preferred stock, which was little changed near $99.

It is the first time the common has traded below the preferred since mid-August. The stock is also down about 20% from its Nov. 10 close near $121.

Strategy added 485 bitcoin last week, lifting its holdings to 850,849 BTC. The shares have kept falling with the bitcoin price. Coinbase was recently down about 3% to about $116. Robinhood (HOOD) and Circle (CRCL) dropped about 4% and 5%.

Bitcoin miners were mostly lower. MARA Holdings (MARA), CleanSpark (CLSK) and IREN (IREN) each fell about 3% to 4%, and Cipher Mining (CIFR) was down about 2%.

Hut 8 (HUT) was a modest exception, recently up about 1%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) were little changed, while Core Scientific (CORZ) and BitMine (BMNR) were also lower.

Nvidia earnings weigh on stocks

The broader market was also weaker late in the session. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was recently down about 1.7%, after falling as much as about 1,000 points, or 2%, at its session low.

The S&P 500 was down about 1.2% and the Nasdaq Composite about 1%.

Nvidia shares were recently down about 1.4%, after falling more than 3% earlier in the session. The chipmaker reports results after the bell, with analysts expecting revenue of about $109 billion. Interim CEO Colette Kress will lead her first earnings call in the role.

Huang, in his first public statement since resigning last week, said he would be “honored” to return as CEO if the board decided it was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America.

Sources told CNBC on Monday that the board is not considering bringing him back. The bitcoin price bounced from its low as Nvidia shares pared some of their losses, and was recently near $64,000.

What comes next for the bitcoin price

New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that the AI investment boom could mean “we may need to raise rates more.” He played down a half-point hike in December. “I don’t think the situation calls for dramatic action,” Williams said.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller did not address the December decision in a payments speech Tuesday. Last week, he said a half-point hike should be considered if October’s core inflation ran at 0.3% or higher, and it did.

Markets still point to a quarter-point increase at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting. Minutes from the October meeting are due Wednesday. The dollar was little changed, still near the 19-month high it touched on Monday.

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $7.9 million on Monday, ending a seven-session outflow streak. Wells Fargo more than doubled its bitcoin ETF stake to $2.35 billion, and Goldman Sachs did the same, lifting its holdings to $1.28 billion.

Anthropic is expected to price its IPO on Wednesday, with shares set to start trading Thursday. A move back above $65,000 would reverse Tuesday’s decline, while a break of the weekend low near $62,000 would put last week’s flush back in view.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $64,000.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: MoneyGram and Solflare Launch USDC Cash-Out at Participating Locations in 170-Plus Markets
summary: A new connection between the Solflare wallet and MoneyGram Ramps aims to solve a practical stablecoin problem: a user can hold digital dollars on Solana but still need.
content:
TL;DR

  • MoneyGram says eligible Solflare users can cash out Solana USDC at participating sites in over 170 markets.
  • A zero-fee launch offer applies through December 31, 2026, under its terms.
  • Coverage, identification rules and payout availability can vary by customer and location.

A new connection between the Solflare wallet and MoneyGram Ramps aims to solve a practical stablecoin problem: a user can hold digital dollars on Solana but still need physical cash. MoneyGram says eligible Solflare users can now withdraw USDC as local currency at participating agent locations in more than 170 countries and territories. That geographic coverage is substantial, but it should not be read as an unconditional cash-out guarantee in every location or for every customer.

The journey from wallet to cash

According to MoneyGram’s November 16 announcement, a Solflare user selects Withdraw, chooses MoneyGram, enters an amount of USDC and follows the guided payout process before collecting cash from a participating outlet. The integration links a self-custody wallet to a familiar physical distribution network. There is still a distinction between initiating a blockchain transfer and receiving funds at the counter: identity verification, local availability and payout requirements can affect completion. Users should rely on the official flow for quotes, instructions and confirmation rather than sending tokens to an address received in an unsolicited message.

A launch promotion has an end date

MoneyGram is promoting zero cash-out fees for eligible Solflare users through December 31, 2026. That is a time-limited offer, not a permanent commitment that every step of a stablecoin withdrawal will be free of all possible costs. Network charges, exchange-rate effects or local requirements may be relevant to a particular transaction, and the published terms and quote should control. The ability to convert tokens into spendable local currency is likely to matter more to many users than a headline about blockchain throughput alone.

For related context, see our earlier report on the latest stablecoin-liquidity developments.

Why physical distribution still counts

Stablecoins move value across digital networks, but they are not universally accepted as a way to pay everyday expenses. MoneyGram’s retail footprint provides a bridge for customers who need banknotes or a locally familiar cash service. The company says its Ramps business has grown substantially and is now being integrated with additional wallets. This arrangement could help cross-border recipients, freelancers or travelers, although actual savings compared with traditional remittance routes will vary by jurisdiction, payment size and the available alternatives.

Self-custody and counterparty handoff

Solflare users retain control of assets in their wallets before initiating a withdrawal, but redeeming those assets involves a service provider and its compliance procedures. That division should be explained clearly to avoid suggesting that a physical cash payout happens without intermediaries. MoneyGram is responsible for relevant payout operations, while the wallet provides access to the flow. The network’s permissionless transfer capabilities and the retail service’s regulated customer requirements are separate parts of the experience. Product reliability will be measured by the success rate of that handoff.

Coverage in a country does not guarantee that every local counter offers the same payout currency, opening hours or amount limits. A traveller should confirm eligibility, identification rules, transaction size, charges and whether the specific location participates before sending any digital asset. Unlike a regular card or bank withdrawal, an on-chain transfer can be irreversible even if a cash pickup is delayed. Clear status messages, refund procedures and support channels will therefore be as important to the product's reputation as the geographical scope of the partner network.

For related context, see our earlier report on a tokenized settlement trial by central banks.

The launch is a concrete use case for dollar stablecoins rather than a broad forecast about adoption. Its significance will depend on where customers can actually collect cash, the all-in cost after promotions end and whether the service remains dependable during high demand.

Reporting sources: MoneyGram launch announcement

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Polish Broker XTB Has Worst Day Since 2021 as Polish Regulator Readies CFD Curbs
summary:
XTB's stock fell 17.5% today (Tuesday) after Poland's financial regulator said it would soon restrict the sale of contracts for difference (CFDs). Those products generate most of the Warsaw-listed broker's revenue.
It was the steepest one-day decline for XTB since July 2021. The shares closed at PLN...
content:
2026-11-17T22:53:00.157+02:00

Tuesday, 17/11/2026 | 20:53 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The watchdog’s deputy chairman said new limits are coming after retail clients lost nearly PLN 2 billion last year.
  • Plus500, IG and CMC slipped about 3% in a broad sell-off, a fraction of the 17.5% slide in Warsaw.

XTB's stock fell 17.5% today (Tuesday) after Poland's financial regulator said it would soon restrict the sale of contracts for difference (CFDs). Those products generate most of the Warsaw-listed broker's revenue.

It was the steepest one-day decline for XTB since July 2021. The shares closed at PLN 115.24, down from PLN 139.72 on Monday, after touching PLN 113.20, a fall of almost 19%. About 3.5 million shares changed hands, nearly seven times the average of the previous 20 sessions.

The broker is more exposed to the measure than most listed rivals. CFDs generated 90.5% of XTB's gross result on financial instruments in the third quarter, even though stocks and ETFs hold most of its clients' money.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Regulator Says 2019 Leverage Caps Fell Short

Dariusz Adamski, deputy chairman of the Polish Financial Supervision Authority (KNF), told a Parkiet newspaper conference in Warsaw that a new product intervention on CFDs would come "soon". He gave no timetable and did not name XTB.

He said 267,000 clients of Polish brokers lost money on CFDs last year, with losses totaling nearly PLN 2 billion (about $500 million), almost seven times the 2019 level. The intervention the KNF introduced that year, which capped leverage , did not have the intended effect, he said.

"In the case of CFDs, the broker becomes not an intermediary but a bookmaker," Adamski said.

The remarks extend a year of pressure from the regulator. In May, Adamski's comments on steering clients from simple products into complex ones sent XTB's stock down more than 8% in a day.

Three months later, the KNF said its review of how brokers sell CFDs remained open, without giving a timetable or possible measures.

Listed Rivals Slipped With the Wider Market

Other listed brokers fell on Tuesday, but by about a sixth as much, in line with a broad sell-off in European equities. Plus500 lost 3.1%, IG Group 3.5% and CMC Markets 2.7% in London, while Swissquote fell 3.1% in Zurich. The STOXX Europe 600 index ended 1.8% lower.

In the third quarter, the same names moved in opposite directions: XTB rose 41.2% while IG fell 27.1% and Plus500 28.5%, FM Intelligence data show.

In Warsaw, Bank Ochrony Środowiska, whose brokerage arm is one of two bank-owned brokers left in Poland's CFD market, slipped 1.7%. The largest of those declines was IG's 3.5%, against XTB's 17.5%.

Only One Regulator-Linked Sell-Off Ran Deeper

Tuesday's fall ranks sixth among XTB's one-day declines since its May 2016 Warsaw listing, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation from daily closing prices. Four of the five larger drops followed quarterly results.

The biggest of those, 31% on July 29, 2020, came when second-quarter profit fell short of the first quarter's. A year later, a quarterly loss cost the stock 21%.

Only one was tied to the regulator. On November 13, 2017, the stock fell 40% after a press report that the KNF had notified prosecutors following an inspection of the broker.

The base is higher this time. Even after Tuesday's slide, XTB stood about 60% above its end-2025 close, though 37% below its record close of PLN 184.16 on August 31.

Mateusz Chrzanowski, an analyst at Noble Securities, told StockWatch that the tone of the regulator's comments could lead investors to price in a negative scenario for XTB's business.

XTB Chief Executive Omar Arnaout has argued that the KNF is more likely to tighten how brokers assess client suitability than to separate CFD and stock accounts. "I think it will end with solutions improving the assessment of client suitability," he told Parkiet TV earlier.

XTB had not commented publicly on Adamski's remarks by the close of trading on Tuesday.

The regulator's last formal step against the broker was a PLN 20 million fine, upheld in a final decision on August 28, over client questionnaires that treated experience with simple instruments as enough to trade CFDs.

Regulator Says 2019 Leverage Caps Fell Short

Dariusz Adamski, deputy chairman of the Polish Financial Supervision Authority (KNF), told a Parkiet newspaper conference in Warsaw that a new product intervention on CFDs would come "soon". He gave no timetable and did not name XTB.

He said 267,000 clients of Polish brokers lost money on CFDs last year, with losses totaling nearly PLN 2 billion (about $500 million), almost seven times the 2019 level. The intervention the KNF introduced that year, which capped leverage , did not have the intended effect, he said.

"In the case of CFDs, the broker becomes not an intermediary but a bookmaker," Adamski said.

The remarks extend a year of pressure from the regulator. In May, Adamski's comments on steering clients from simple products into complex ones sent XTB's stock down more than 8% in a day.

Three months later, the KNF said its review of how brokers sell CFDs remained open, without giving a timetable or possible measures.

Listed Rivals Slipped With the Wider Market

Other listed brokers fell on Tuesday, but by about a sixth as much, in line with a broad sell-off in European equities. Plus500 lost 3.1%, IG Group 3.5% and CMC Markets 2.7% in London, while Swissquote fell 3.1% in Zurich. The STOXX Europe 600 index ended 1.8% lower.

In the third quarter, the same names moved in opposite directions: XTB rose 41.2% while IG fell 27.1% and Plus500 28.5%, FM Intelligence data show.

In Warsaw, Bank Ochrony Środowiska, whose brokerage arm is one of two bank-owned brokers left in Poland's CFD market, slipped 1.7%. The largest of those declines was IG's 3.5%, against XTB's 17.5%.

Only One Regulator-Linked Sell-Off Ran Deeper

Tuesday's fall ranks sixth among XTB's one-day declines since its May 2016 Warsaw listing, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation from daily closing prices. Four of the five larger drops followed quarterly results.

The biggest of those, 31% on July 29, 2020, came when second-quarter profit fell short of the first quarter's. A year later, a quarterly loss cost the stock 21%.

Only one was tied to the regulator. On November 13, 2017, the stock fell 40% after a press report that the KNF had notified prosecutors following an inspection of the broker.

The base is higher this time. Even after Tuesday's slide, XTB stood about 60% above its end-2025 close, though 37% below its record close of PLN 184.16 on August 31.

Mateusz Chrzanowski, an analyst at Noble Securities, told StockWatch that the tone of the regulator's comments could lead investors to price in a negative scenario for XTB's business.

XTB Chief Executive Omar Arnaout has argued that the KNF is more likely to tighten how brokers assess client suitability than to separate CFD and stock accounts. "I think it will end with solutions improving the assessment of client suitability," he told Parkiet TV earlier.

XTB had not commented publicly on Adamski's remarks by the close of trading on Tuesday.

The regulator's last formal step against the broker was a PLN 20 million fine, upheld in a final decision on August 28, over client questionnaires that treated experience with simple instruments as enough to trade CFDs.

title: Eastern Europe crypto flows fall 7.9% as Ukraine draws $12B in stablecoins
summary: Chainalysis found that Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in crypto activity of any region, while cross-border stablecoin transfers to Ukraine continued amid the ongoing war.
content:
Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in cryptocurrency activity among the regions tracked by Chainalysis in the year ended June 2026, falling 7.9% even as retail-sized transfers increased in value, according to a report published Tuesday.

The region’s crypto economy shrank to $642.1 billion from $697.1 billion a year earlier, compared with a 1.6% decline globally, the report states. Russia, which accounted for roughly 44% of the regional total, saw activity fall 14.7% to $284.1 billion over the period. By contrast, Belarus recorded 27.6% growth, while Bulgaria, Moldova and Ukraine saw smaller increases.

The value of transfers of $10,000 or more to crypto services fell 17.4%, from $591.5 billion to $488.6 billion, according to the report.

The value of smaller transfers to crypto services, meanwhile, rose 8.3%. These retail-sized transfers accounted for 13.1% of the value sent to crypto services in Eastern Europe, the highest share of any region studied and above the global average of 10.1%.

Eastern European crypto activity by country, July 2025 to June 2026. Source: Chainalysis report

Polish crypto ATM activity grows

Crypto ATM activity also increased across Eastern Europe, with transaction volumes nearly doubling from $17.3 million to $33.9 million. Poland recorded a 120% increase in ATM transactions despite a 5% decline in centralized exchange activity, with stablecoins accounting for roughly 90% of its ATM transactions.

Chainalysis measures the crypto economy using inflows to crypto services, domestic transfers between personal wallets and cross-border inflows to personal wallets. The figures are measured in dollars, so cryptocurrency price changes can also affect the totals, according to its methodology.

Related: OpenPayd secures MiCA license as stablecoin adoption grows in Europe

Ukraine receives billions in stablecoins

Despite the broader regional decline, Ukraine remained a major destination for stablecoins, receiving $12 billion in cross-border wallet-to-wallet transfers. Of that, $2.41 billion was in retail-sized transfers below $10,000, according to Chainalysis.

Chainalysis also found that countries with larger Ukrainian populations, including prewar diaspora communities and refugees who arrived after Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, generally sent more stablecoins to Ukraine. Among the 36 countries studied across Europe and North America,

Canada was the largest source of retail-sized, remittance-like transfers, at $359 million.

Crypto transfers to Ukraine by diaspora population, July 2025 to June 2026. Source: Chainalysis report

A Chainalysis spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the cross-border flows were largely denominated in US dollar-pegged stablecoins, although the firm did not provide a breakdown by individual token.

title: Kalshi Axes Trump Mention Markets After CFTC Raises Concerns: CNBC
summary: Prediction market operator Kalshi has suspended several contracts allowing traders to wager on President Donald Trump’s choice of words after federal regulators intervened, extending a crackdown on a controversial betting category previously linked to insider trading at the White House. The company ...
content:
Prediction market operator Kalshi has suspended several contracts allowing traders to wager on President Donald Trump’s choice of words after federal regulators intervened, extending a crackdown on a controversial betting category previously linked to insider trading at the White House.

Key Takeaways

  • Kalshi suspended several Trump-related prediction markets following a CFTC directive, citing concerns that wagers on the president’s choice of words could be manipulated or exploited by insiders.
  • The crackdown follows an insider trading scandal involving a former White House teleprompter operator who reportedly earned roughly $100,000 betting on Trump’s remarks. Kalshi previously eliminated sports-related mention markets amid similar concerns.
  • The CFTC’s intervention highlights its dual approach to prediction markets: defending federal oversight against state gambling regulators while restricting contracts vulnerable to manipulation.

The company stopped trading in several Trump-related markets late last week following a request from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), according to a Tuesday CNBC report. The affected contracts included wagers on which nicknames Trump might use before the end of 2026, which subjects he would mention during November, and which countries and corporations he might reference before the month concludes.

The intervention follows months of regulatory scrutiny surrounding so-called mention markets, which allow participants to speculate on particular words or expressions appearing in speeches, television appearances, and corporate earnings calls.

Unlike contracts tied to broader political or economic outcomes, these markets can be influenced directly by the person speaking or by individuals with advance knowledge of prepared remarks, creating opportunities for insider trading and deliberate manipulation.

CFTC spokesperson Brooke Nethercott told CNBC that the agency had suspended the certification of certain Kalshi contracts because of concerns about their vulnerability to manipulation. At least one affected contract had originally been self-certified by the exchange in Feb. 2025.

Kalshi spokesperson Dani Lever confirmed that the company was complying with the regulator’s directive. The suspension does not extend to all mention markets, with a contract involving Vice President JD Vance’s upcoming appearance at the New York Times DealBook Summit remaining available Tuesday.

White House Insider Trading Scandal Fuels Scrutiny

The latest action follows a high-profile enforcement case involving Gabriel Perez, a former White House teleprompter operator who used his access to Trump’s prepared speeches to profit from prediction market contracts.

As previously reported by Bitcoin.com News, Perez correctly predicted the outcomes of 39 of 43 contracts involving Trump’s remarks, generating roughly $100,000 in trading profits. The CFTC subsequently ordered him to surrender his gains, imposed a financial penalty and prohibited him from trading on regulated markets for three years.

The case demonstrated how individuals with privileged access to information could exploit markets whose outcomes depend on the precise language used by public officials. The regulator had already taken steps to restrict the category. In August, Kalshi eliminated its sports-related mention markets amid a CFTC review examining whether such contracts could be manipulated.

Bitcoin.com News reported at the time that political and corporate mention markets remained available despite the sports-related removals. Trump-related contracts accounted for a substantial majority of the trading volume in the remaining mention markets examined at the time.

The CFTC subsequently warned exchanges in September about the elevated manipulation risks associated with these products, setting the stage for its latest intervention.

Regulatory Pressure Grows Despite CFTC Support for Prediction Markets

The restrictions come as Kalshi faces mounting legal and political challenges, even as the CFTC has generally defended the authority of federally regulated prediction exchanges to operate nationwide.

Last week, the CFTC and Department of Justice sued Arkansas to prevent state authorities from enforcing gambling regulations against Kalshi. The federal government argues that prediction market contracts offered through CFTC-regulated exchanges fall under federal commodities law rather than individual state gambling statutes.

As Bitcoin.com News reported, Arkansas is among numerous states challenging prediction market operators over contracts that state officials characterize as unlicensed gambling products.

Kalshi has also faced growing political scrutiny over its connections to the Trump family. Donald Trump Jr. recently departed his advisory position with the company after his investment firm, 1789 Capital, committed substantial funding to rival prediction market platform Polymarket.

His departure comes as congressional Democrats prepare to investigate the Trump family’s financial interests in cryptocurrency and prediction markets following their victory in the November midterm elections.

The latest CFTC intervention illustrates an important distinction in the regulator’s approach: While the agency has aggressively defended federal jurisdiction over prediction markets, it is simultaneously restricting individual products that it believes pose unacceptable risks to market integrity.

Kalshi, meanwhile, continues to defend the economic value of mention markets, arguing that statements from influential public figures can move financial markets and therefore represent legitimate subjects for event contracts.

The company is also facing a separate CFTC investigation into its communications with regulators about proposed new products, CNBC reported. Kalshi said it was working to address those concerns.

The fate of the suspended Trump contracts remains uncertain as the regulator continues examining whether the exchange can adequately protect these markets against manipulation.

title: ‘Bought the Dip’: Twenty One Capital Adds 154 Bitcoin for $10M
summary: Twenty One Capital spent about $10 million in cash to buy 154.32 bitcoin as BTC hovered below $65,000. The purchase lifts its treasury to 43,668 BTC and reinforces the company’s capital allocation decision to simply buy more bitcoin. Twenty One Says Volatility Created a $10M Bitcoin Opportunity Twen...
content:
Twenty One Capital spent about $10 million in cash to buy 154.32 bitcoin as BTC hovered below $65,000. The purchase lifts its treasury to 43,668 BTC and reinforces the company’s capital allocation decision to simply buy more bitcoin.

Key Takeaways

  • Twenty One Capital bought 154.32 BTC for about $10M, lifting holdings to roughly 43,668 BTC.
  • CEO Rapha Zagury says every investment must beat the expected return from simply buying more bitcoin.
  • Lower BTC prices make alternative uses of cash harder to justify under Twenty One’s capital-allocation model.

Twenty One Says Volatility Created a $10M Bitcoin Opportunity

Twenty One Capital is treating bitcoin’s latest sell-off as an opportunity rather than a warning.

The NYSE-listed company purchased 154.32 BTC for approximately $10 million, paying an average of $64,801.01 per bitcoin. The cash-funded acquisition increased Twenty One Capital’s holdings to about 43,668 BTC as of Nov. 16—a sum recently valued near $2.8 billion.

“We built Twenty One because we believe in bitcoin. That conviction doesn’t change with the price. Volatility creates opportunities. We saw one, acted, and bought the dip,” said Twenty One CEO Rapha Zagury.

The move comes as bitcoin has suffered a sharp correction, testing the conviction of corporate treasury companies that accumulated crypto at higher prices.

Bitcoin Becomes the Hurdle Rate for Every Investment

CEO Rapha Zagury added that Twenty One Capital now compares potential acquisitions directly against the expected value of purchasing additional bitcoin. He commented:

Bitcoin is our benchmark for every investment decision we make. Any business we acquire has to beat simply buying more bitcoin, and this weekend’s drop in price made adding bitcoin an easy decision.

That framework gives Twenty One an unusually high hurdle for deploying cash elsewhere.

The company’s Nov. 13 shareholder letter outlined plans to build cash-generating businesses around its bitcoin treasury. Those businesses must produce surplus cash after operating expenses, reinvestment, and financing costs, creating additional capital that could ultimately support further BTC accumulation.

Saylor Backs Twenty One’s Dip-Buying Conviction

Strategy co-founder and Executive Chairman Michael Saylor, whose company pioneered the corporate bitcoin treasury model and currently sits on about $55 billion worth of BTC, applauded the purchase.

“Conviction doesn’t change with the price. Well done, Twenty One,” Saylor wrote in response to Zagury.

Twenty One said future purchases will depend on market conditions, liquidity, and competing investment opportunities.

That qualification matters. Corporate bitcoin strategies face their biggest test when prices fall, and capital becomes harder to raise.

For Twenty One, however, the message from this purchase is straightforward: bitcoin remains the benchmark, and lower prices make that benchmark harder for other investments to beat.

Last week, the firm reported its first profitable quarter since going public in 2025, posting $1.09 billion in third-quarter net income, largely from unrealized bitcoin gains. However, operating cash flow remained negative, highlighting challenges in generating sustainable revenue. The company is exploring mining, lending, and other bitcoin-related businesses while managing $486.5 million in debt.

Situational Awareness, the artificial intelligence hedge fund run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, cut its bitcoin miner holdings sharply in the third quarter, leaving about $80.8 million across three stocks and exiting three others, a Monday filing shows.

The San Francisco firm still held 3,019,029 CleanSpark shares, worth $38.9 million at Sept. 30, 1,934,618 Bitdeer shares, worth $20.3 million, and 527,864 IREN shares, worth $21.6 million. Those are the only miner lines left, a sliver of the $1.83 billion in six miner stocks the fund listed at June 30.

IREN Cut 94%, and three miners are gone

The deepest cut was IREN. The fund held 9,474,099 IREN shares, worth $433.3 million, at midyear. The Sept. 30 stake is about 94% smaller by share count. CleanSpark was trimmed about 75%, from 12,276,139 shares worth $178.6 million. Bitdeer was reduced about 44%, from 3,439,450 shares worth $54.6 million. Bitdeer’s reported value fell further than its share count, to $20.3 million, as the stock also declined.

Three names disappeared from the filing entirely. The fund had held 26,008,473 Core Scientific shares, worth $665.6 million, 17,100,000 Riot Platforms shares, worth $468.2 million, and 9,133,726 Hive Digital shares, worth $33.2 million, at June 30. None of those lines appear in the new report. The filing does not say whether those sales were part of a late-July portfolio sale, later trades, or both.

An AI thesis that ran through Bitcoin miners

Aschenbrenner published a long 2024 essay, “Situational Awareness: The Decade Ahead,” arguing that artificial general intelligence was approaching faster than most investors appreciated, and that computing power and electricity would be the tight constraints. He founded the fund that September around that view, looking at technology and energy companies that AI would help or hurt.

The miner stakes fit the same idea. A March profile described the fund as betting that electricity and computing capacity may be the most valuable assets in the AI build-out, pointing to miners that were turning high-density facilities and power contracts toward AI workloads. IREN has signed a multiyear cloud contract with Microsoft. CleanSpark has struck a $6.6 billion data-center lease. Listed miners have also been operating under tight economics this year, with bitcoin often trading below estimated production costs.

A July sale to Citadel, then a much smaller filing

The cuts landed after a brutal July. The fund sold the bulk of the fund’s public stock portfolio to Ken Griffin’s Citadel late that month after heavy losses on AI-related holdings, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Those sources said the fund was forced to unwind most of its public book. In a letter to investors, Aschenbrenner said the portfolio was down an estimated 67% in July, that the fund had come “closer to permanent capital impairment than is acceptable,” and that it had sold a portion of its public holdings in a block trade to remove all leverage and close its shorts. The unaudited letter still put year-to-date performance at plus 80%. Aschenbrenner said the fund was not shutting down and had preserved its private investments.

The new 13F shows how much of the public book was left by Sept. 30. Reported long holdings fell from $20.24 billion, across 26 lines, at June 30, to $1.58 billion, across 23 lines, three months later. That decline should not be read as the fund losing 92% of its capital. A 13F reports only long positions in U.S.-listed stocks and certain options. It leaves out cash, shorts and private investments, and option lines are valued at the underlying shares, not the premiums paid. Reuters’ sources said that after the Citadel deal the fund would hold a book of roughly $10 billion, including stocks and private investments such as a stake in Anthropic.

What remains is concentrated. The largest common-stock line is now SharonAI, 8,070,950 shares worth $440.7 million. Aschenbrenner also listed call options on Bloom Energy, SanDisk, Nebius and a memory ETF. The three leftover miner stakes are a stub of the midyear book. Whether those positions were trimmed further after Sept. 30 will only be clear when the fourth-quarter 13F arrives in mid-February.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Lighter incident exposes risks beyond withdrawal controls
summary: Crypto platforms need enforceable limits on every route an API key can use to transfer value, including trades, internal transfers and shared pools.
content:
A recent incident where over $10 million was siphoned out of a decentralized perpetual futures exchange shows the shortcomings of focusing security on withdrawal controls

According to Lighter’s postmortem, an attacker used compromised API keys to move funds into a public pool and redeem shares held through another account. Bitquery traced a withdrawal of 10.39 million USDC. The exchange said its protocol and smart contracts were unaffected.

Lighter now requires wallet signatures for transfers into public pools and has made API-key signatures non-public. It also plans IP allowlists and configurable permissions for individual keys.

Lighter has since restored deposits and withdrawals while also returning about $5 million in USDC (USDC) to the affected trader.

Lighter incident infographic. Source: Bitquery

The incident highlights how cybersecurity reviews need to look past smart contract vulnerabilities. It is important to also consider the gap between the permissions a system grants and the financial consequences those permissions allow.

Related: Google says hackers use AI agents to find and exploit software flaws

The real risk involving a credential depends on the balances it can reach, the transactions it can initiate and the exposures it can create. Whether it is permitted to withdraw assets and to which destinations are just two of many factors. As Lighter put it in its postmortem:

“A key that can trade can still lose you money if someone else holds it.”

This means that a user needs to establish a clear mandate for each credential. The mandate can specify accessible accounts, permitted markets, order sizes, pricing tolerances and aggregate exposure. Moving capital into a shared pool or expanding those limits can require separate authorization.

The same logic applies to additional signatures. A second signature adds meaningful protection when its approval process independently evaluates the transaction’s financial effect.

title: Fed’s Waller cites Binance hack in warning over tokenized finance
summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller questioned who bears responsibility for fraud, compromised keys and failed transactions as traditional financial assets move onto blockchains.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 17, 2026

Fed Governor Christopher Waller questioned who bears responsibility for fraud, compromised keys and failed transactions as traditional financial assets move onto blockchains.

US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller cited the recent $6.3 billion Binance hack while raising questions about security and accountability in tokenized financial markets, suggesting that major institutional transactions may require blockchain systems offering greater privacy and control.

Speaking at The Clearing House’s annual conference in New York on Nov. 17, an event bringing together banking and payments industry leaders, Waller questioned who would bear responsibility when fraudsters exploit smart contracts, private keys are compromised, transfers go wrong or assets become stranded on failed blockchains.

Waller said the level of security and oversight required could depend on the importance of the financial transactions involved:

For example, systemically important financial transactions may call for the most conservative designs. These designs might trade some of the developer creativity found on purely permissionless, open networks in favor of greater privacy and control.

The expansion of tokenized finance would also require clear legal frameworks governing ownership rights, custody and settlement, he said, arguing that governance and legal protections are as important as technical safeguards in building trust.

Waller’s remarks came as four Democratic senators pressed the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) over safeguards for tokenized stocks. In a letter released Monday, the lawmakers questioned who would be responsible for shares transferred outside regulated platforms and whether regulators could freeze or recover the tokens.

Related: Custodia Bank loses Supreme Court bid for direct Fed payment access

Barr warns of AI-related cybersecurity risks

Waller wasn’t the only Federal Reserve governor to raise concerns about emerging financial technologies this week. His remarks followed a Monday speech by fellow Fed Governor Michael Barr, who warned that artificial intelligence could introduce new cybersecurity risks as financial institutions increasingly adopt the technology.

Barr said AI-enabled attackers were exploiting vulnerabilities previously considered too difficult to target, while autonomous AI systems could behave in ways that undermine security controls

“Attackers only need to be right once, while defenders need to be right all the time,” Barr said.

He also said major banks had reported finding AI agents attempting to take actions in retail customer accounts without being able to verify their authenticity or authorization, highlighting the need for stronger authentication and security controls.

title: Nvidia AI Chip Restrictions Expand as US Closes Cloud Computing Loophole for China
summary: The United States is tightening restrictions on advanced AI chip exports, targeting overseas data centers that allow Chinese companies to access restricted computing power remotely.
content:
Skip to content

The United States is tightening restrictions on advanced AI chip exports, targeting overseas data centers that allow Chinese companies to access restricted computing power remotely.

The Commerce Department’s latest measures extend existing semiconductor controls to cloud infrastructure, adding pressure on Nvidia’s international supply chain and escalating tensions between Washington and Beijing.

US Targets Remote Access to Advanced AI Chips

The US Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule on November 16, 2026, aimed at preventing companies in China and other restricted jurisdictions from accessing advanced American computing technology through overseas data centers.

The US is tightening controls on remote access to advanced AI chips by Chinese firms through overseas data centers. Source: @AFP via X

Previously, US export controls primarily focused on the physical shipment of advanced semiconductors. However, companies could potentially bypass these restrictions by renting computing capacity from data centers operating in countries outside the direct scope of the controls.

The new rule addresses this gap by requiring licenses for exports, reexports, or domestic transfers of covered advanced semiconductors and related equipment intended for data centers providing significant computing capacity to companies headquartered in China, Macau, or other designated restricted jurisdictions.

The regulation establishes a threshold of 12 million aggregate Total Processing Performance (TPP) for computing access across individual or digitally connected data centers. It also covers indirect arrangements involving third-party operators and intermediaries.

Under the new requirements, data center operators, foreign chip manufacturers, and exporters must conduct customer due diligence to identify the ultimate users of advanced computing infrastructure. This includes examining direct and indirect ownership structures to determine whether restricted entities control or benefit from the services.

The BIS said the measure would ensure existing restrictions could not be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries.

Five Countries Face Additional Export Licensing Requirements

The US has also expanded its export licensing requirements to five countries identified as higher-risk destinations for semiconductor diversion.

The list includes Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil. Companies exporting, reexporting, or transferring covered advanced semiconductors to these markets will face additional licensing requirements under the updated framework.

The US is tightening AI chip export controls, requiring licenses for transfers to high-risk countries and setting a 12 million TPP computing threshold for data centers serving restricted entities. Source: @StockMKTNewz/X

The decision reflects concerns that restricted chips could reach unauthorized destinations through intermediaries, overseas cloud providers, or complex supply-chain arrangements.

However, the rules include an exception for shipments intended for companies headquartered in the United States or whose ultimate parent companies are based there, provided exporters meet the applicable reporting requirements.

Existing overseas data centers that already provide significant computing capacity to restricted companies will have 90 days from the rule’s effective date to obtain the necessary licenses if they intend to continue those services.

The regulation also excludes commercial recommendation systems used by online retailers and social media platforms, provided they meet the specific requirements. These systems generally rank, filter, or recommend products and content rather than generate new AI models or content.

The measures are part of a broader effort to extend US export controls beyond physical semiconductor shipments and cover the computing infrastructure that enables advanced AI development.

Megaspeed Investigation Adds Pressure on Nvidia

The regulatory changes follow growing scrutiny of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International, which has been investigated over suspected violations of US semiconductor export controls.

The US Commerce and Justice departments confirmed on November 16 that the investigation began in 2024 after authorities identified suspicious activity involving potential semiconductor diversion.

According to their joint statement, Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia in May 2025 concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed. Nvidia subsequently placed the company on its internal no-sell list in June 2025.

US investigators, working alongside Singaporean law enforcement officials, conducted an on-site inspection at Megaspeed that same month and interviewed its then-chief executive, Alice Huang. The Justice Department later assumed the lead role in the criminal investigation.

The case attracted additional attention following reports about Alice Huang’s relationship with Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang and allegations concerning her possible links to Chinese intelligence. Those allegations have not been established as criminal findings in the government’s public statement.

Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s chief executive on November 12, 2026, amid growing scrutiny surrounding the controversy.

The investigation has highlighted how overseas cloud infrastructure can potentially provide access to advanced Nvidia processors without requiring restricted chips to be physically shipped into China.

The latest Commerce Department measures directly address this type of arrangement by extending licensing requirements to data centers that provide computing capacity to restricted customers.

China Warns of Countermeasures as AI Trade Tensions Escalate

Beijing has strongly opposed Washington’s latest export restrictions, warning that it could introduce countermeasures if the United States proceeds with the new controls.

China’s Commerce Ministry said on November 17 that it firmly opposed the measure, arguing that it further restricts Chinese companies’ access to advanced AI chips from manufacturers such as Nvidia.

China warned it would take “necessary measures” and retaliatory action in response to the new US AI chip export restrictions. Source: @Polymarket/X

The ministry also called on Washington to return to the “correct track” of resolving differences through consultation and cooperation.

The response adds another layer of tension to the technology and trade relationship between the world’s two largest economies. The announcement also comes ahead of a planned meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

Meanwhile, US lawmakers are considering additional legislation to strengthen oversight of advanced semiconductor exports and address remote access to restricted computing resources.

Several proposals seek to expand congressional oversight of chip export licenses and improve tracking mechanisms to prevent advanced processors from reaching unauthorized destinations. These efforts could further shape US semiconductor policy in 2027.

A Polymarket prediction market placed the probability of a related AI chip export licensing bill becoming law in 2026 at 45%. The figure reflects traders’ expectations rather than an official legislative forecast or confirmed outcome.

Chinese AI Stocks Decline as Chip Access Concerns Grow

The latest restrictions have also weighed on investor sentiment toward China’s artificial intelligence sector.

Chinese technology stocks declined on November 17 as investors assessed the potential impact of tighter access to advanced computing infrastructure.

Bloomberg data shows mounting losses in major Chinese tech stocks, including Alibaba, Tencent, and Baidu, accelerating in mid-November amid AI computing access concerns. Source: @GlobalMktObserv/X

Alibaba shares fell approximately 5%, while Baidu declined 5.8% to a record low. AI model developers MiniMax and Z.AI also recorded losses exceeding 5%, while robotics company Yushu Technology dropped around 12%.

The declines contributed to a 1.1% fall in the Hang Seng Tech Index, reflecting concerns about the potential impact of US semiconductor restrictions on Chinese cloud providers and AI developers.

However, the market reaction was not uniform across the semiconductor industry. Chinese chipmakers Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC) and Hua Hong Semiconductor gained as investors considered the possibility of increased demand for domestically produced chips.

The divergence highlights the potential consequences of tighter US export controls for China’s technology industry. While companies dependent on advanced foreign processors could face higher computing costs and infrastructure constraints, domestic semiconductor manufacturers may benefit from efforts to reduce reliance on overseas suppliers.

The latest restrictions therefore extend beyond Nvidia’s chip sales, potentially affecting cloud computing providers, AI developers, semiconductor manufacturers, and data center operators across multiple markets.

For Nvidia, the regulatory changes introduce additional compliance requirements for international customers and distribution partners. For China, they create another obstacle in securing the computing resources needed to develop increasingly sophisticated AI systems.
