title: Coinbase Launches ChatGPT Plugin for Trading Bitcoin, Stocks, and Derivatives
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Coinbase Launches ChatGPT Plugin for Trading Bitcoin, Stocks, and Derivatives
Coinbase launched an official ChatGPT plugin Tuesday that lets users connect an account and trade bitcoin, other crypto, stocks and derivatives in the chat, approving every order. The official plugin is c...
content:
Coinbase launched an official plugin for ChatGPT on Tuesday that lets users connect a Coinbase account and trade bitcoin, other cryptocurrencies, stocks and derivatives without leaving the conversation, provided they approve every order.

The company said the tool puts trading “in the same chat you use for everything else.” Users can connect an account, review a portfolio and place orders from ChatGPT on the web, on mobile or on desktop. Chief executive Brian Armstrong wrote that “starting today anyone with ChatGPT can connect their Coinbase account” and can “trade right inside your Coinbase account.”

Coinbase posted a link to the official plugin in ChatGPT’s directory. Its developer documentation describes a short setup: sign in, review the access being requested and choose which portfolios the plugin can see. Interactive confirmation cards in the chat cover new orders, edits, cancellations and conversions between dollars and USDC. Read-only requests, such as checking a balance, do not use them.

Bitcoin, Stocks and Dated Futures, With a Card on Every Trade

The announcement did not single out bitcoin, but the plugin sits on the same rails as Coinbase for Agents, the company’s toolkit for connecting AI apps to a trading account. That documentation lists spot trading in more than 900 pairs, including bitcoin, along with eligible U.S. stocks and dated futures from Coinbase Financial Markets. The examples include a market buy of bitcoin and a dated bitcoin futures contract. Orders go through Advanced Trade, so those fees and eligibility rules apply. Fees vary by product, fee tier and whether an order adds or takes liquidity, and they are shown on the order preview.

The official plugin is narrower than the full agent toolkit. A separate custom connection is required for the company’s Global Derivatives products and for x402 payments, which agents can use to buy market data. Coinbase already offers U.S. customers stock and ETF trading on its own platform, but the agent documentation says equity orders trade during regular market hours by default. The plugin should not be read as a new around-the-clock stock venue. What a user can buy still depends on the products already attached to that account.

Official Access Is Limited to U.S. Coinbase Users

Armstrong’s “anyone with ChatGPT” line is broader than the documentation. The official plugin is currently available to U.S. Coinbase users, and availability also depends on a user’s ChatGPT account and workspace. If the plugin does not appear, the company tells users to check their workspace’s plugin policy. In a disclaimer attached to Tuesday’s announcement, it said product availability, eligibility and Coinbase entities “vary by jurisdiction,” that trading can result in a total loss, and that “AI agents may fail.”

The same post said users direct all AI activity and assume full responsibility. The developer documentation adds that agents can misinterpret instructions or produce inaccurate output, and that the user is responsible for reviewing and authorizing trades. Access can be revoked later in an account’s security settings, under connections.

OpenAI’s help pages describe a distinct Finances feature in the United States that can connect bank and credit-report data but cannot place trades, and note that third-party plugins that support transactions are a separate product.

A Consumer Layer on Tools Coinbase Built This Year

Tuesday’s plugin is the most visible version of work the company has been shipping for months. In June, it introduced Coinbase for Agents, a login and a command-line tool that let an AI app trade inside limits set by the user, including a gradual rebalancing toward a bitcoin-heavy portfolio. On Nov. 11, it added Agent Controls, server-side caps on trade size and 24-hour volume, plus an auto-stop if a portfolio falls by a set percentage. Those controls live on the company’s servers, so an agent cannot switch them off.

The official plugin is meant for people who want to stay in the loop. The company also documents a custom ChatGPT connection for automated workflows that does not add a confirmation card before each trade, though sign-in, consent and authorization for financial actions still apply. For the official plugin, every bitcoin, stock or derivatives order still needs a human yes.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders as Customers Report Scam Calls
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders as Customers Report Scam Calls
A breach at shipping partner Skladon exposed names, addresses, emails, phone numbers and purchase details for about 27,000 Trezor orders, the company said, and some customers have already reported s...
content:
Trezor said Monday that a data breach at Skladon, one of its shipping partners, exposed personal information tied to about 27,000 hardware-wallet orders, and that some customers have already reported scam calls. The company’s own systems were not compromised, and no wallet backups, PINs or passphrases were involved.

Skladon notified Trezor on Nov. 15 of unauthorized access to systems that held customer shipping data. The breach itself took place on Nov. 7. Trezor believes the attacker exported records for orders placed between Aug. 9 and Nov. 7. An investigation is ongoing.

Names, addresses and purchase details were leaked

The exposed records included full names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, email addresses, order dates, and the products purchased and their prices. Trezor said neither it nor Skladon ever holds wallet backups, PINs or passphrases, so the breach does not, by itself, let an attacker move a buyer’s bitcoin. It does give a stranger a home address and proof that the person bought a device designed to store crypto.

Anyone who received Trezor’s incident email and ordered in that window was affected. A small number of customers who ordered between Aug. 9 and 14 may also be included, but the company cannot email them because those details had already been anonymized under its 90-day retention policy. It is reaching those buyers through its blog and posted the same warning on X. Skladon does not ship to the United States, Trezor said, so U.S. customers were not affected by this incident. The company added that Skladon delivers to many countries, and that the leak is not limited to one region.

Trezor warns of scam calls

Trezor told customers to treat any unexpected call, text, email or letter about their order as suspicious, and to be alert to potential risks to their physical security. Scammers may quote real order details, including what was bought and what was paid, to make a message look genuine. Some customers have already reported scam calls.

“Trezor will never cold-call you or ask for your wallet backup,” the company said. Customers should contact support only through the company’s website, never through a link, QR code or number in an unsolicited message, and should never enter a wallet backup anywhere except on their device. If a message contains a threat or makes someone feel unsafe, Trezor said to contact local police first.

The third partner incident this year

This is not the first time a Trezor contractor has lost customer data. In August, a breach at shipping provider ShipMonk exposed records from 13,689 customers, including 11,742 with full names, emails, phone numbers and shipping addresses. Trezor later said another approximately 67,000 U.S. customers who ordered between November 2019 and August 2021 were also affected, after ShipMonk failed to delete records it had assured the company were gone.

In September, a breach at marketing platform Brevo let an attacker send a phishing email through Trezor’s account and, the company later confirmed, export 347,149 newsletter addresses. Trezor took down the malicious domain within 20 minutes, but about 2,500 people had already clicked the link.

“We know this is not the first time customer contact details and addresses have been exposed in an incident involving one of our partners,” Trezor said Monday, adding that it is sorry, especially to anyone affected again. Hardware-wallet makers have faced this risk before. In 2020, an unauthorized party accessed Ledger’s e-commerce and marketing database, leaking over 1 million email addresses; Bitcoin Magazine later reported that more than 200,000 people also had home addresses exposed, and that some victims were later mailed fake devices.

In response, Trezor said anonymous pickup is now available in 18 European countries, so a name and home address need not reach the company, and that it is working to launch the option in the United States. It is also cutting how long it keeps order data from 90 days to 45, with plans to reduce that period further, and it has informed the data protection authority. The company said it is reviewing its relationships with third-party partners and the security requirements it places on them.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Kalshi Flags 50+ Insider Trading Cases as Surveillance Closes In on Leaked Events
summary:
Kalshi made more than 50 referrals to law enforcement concerning suspected insider trading in the second and third quarters. Yet an outside review found that markets accounting for about 98% of its trading volume carried a lower risk of access to material non-public information. 
Kalshi now plans to...
content:
2026-11-17T18:07:30.119+02:00

Tuesday, 17/11/2026 | 16:07 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • An independent committee classified markets representing about 98% of trading volume as lower risk for access to material non-public information.
  • Market risk ratings and trading histories will guide alert thresholds, aiming to focus surveillance where private knowledge could matter.

Kalshi made more than 50 referrals to law enforcement concerning suspected insider trading in the second and third quarters. Yet an outside review found that markets accounting for about 98% of its trading volume carried a lower risk of access to material non-public information.

Kalshi now plans to direct more of its surveillance capacity towards contracts where advance knowledge could give a trader an advantage, according to the exchange’s announcement.

When a Trader Knows Before the Market

A football score or published crypto price becomes known as events unfold, but a company’s decision to launch a token may be known internally before an announcement, meaning that someone with that information could take a position before other traders can account for it in the contract’s price.

The risk has already appeared in cases involving very different events. In 2025, Kalshi investigated an editor for a YouTube channel whose trades on contracts linked to its videos had been unusually successful.

Kalshi concluded that the editor likely had advance access to unpublished content and suspended the trader for two years, according to a CFTC enforcement advisory.

A separate case reached criminal court in April. US prosecutors charged an Army soldier with allegedly using classified information about a military operation in Venezuela to make approximately $410,000 on Polymarket contracts.

The allegations concern another platform, but show why exchanges need to examine who may have known about an event before trading on it.

Who Reviewed Kalshi’s Surveillance

The outside committee, announced by Kalshi in February, now consists of Daniel Taylor, a Wharton professor who directs its Forensic Analytics Lab, and Lisa Pinheiro, a managing principal at Analysis Group. They test how Kalshi spots suspicious trading and recommend changes; Kalshi’s staff investigate traders and make referrals.

For its latest review, the committee analysed anonymised data from 500 million historical trades and nearly 900,000 surveillance alerts. It also rebuilt past order books from more than 44 billion updates.

Taylor said he was “impressed by the extent of overlap” between activity his team flagged and cases Kalshi had already investigated, acted on or referred to the CFTC.

The experts also found that Kalshi sometimes puts contracts with different insider risks in the same category. Its crypto “pre-market” category covers both a company’s possible token launch and what the token might be worth at a future date.

People inside the company may know its launch plans; the future price has yet to be set by trading. Pinheiro said, “Even markets within the same broad category can differ substantially.”

The committee identified 21 subcategories that need this kind of closer classification.

What Kalshi Will Change

Kalshi already assigns risk scores to certain markets. Under measures introduced in June, it also began collecting employment information from traders in higher-risk markets to screen for potential insiders before they trade.

Now Kalshi plans to separate markets with different risk profiles, then use their trading histories to calibrate alert thresholds. More of its review capacity would go to markets exposed to advance knowledge, while lower-risk markets should produce fewer false alarms.

Technology providers support other parts of that work. Kalshi partnered with Solidus Labs on trade-surveillance tools in February and announced a phased rollout of Nasdaq Market Surveillance in August.

The committee examined whether a trader’s profits and win rate across several markets could reveal suspicious activity missed by an alert on a single trade. Its next review will move beyond trading on non-public information to other forms of market abuse, including spoofing.

title: Wells Fargo More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Stake to $2.35 Billion
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Wells Fargo More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Stake to $2.35 Billion
Wells Fargo's third-quarter 13F shows 49.6 million IBIT shares worth $2.35 billion at Sept. 30, up from 24.4 million, while its Strategy stake fell about 33% to 1.34 million shares.
This post Wells Fargo More Than...
content:
Wells Fargo more than doubled its holdings of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust in the third quarter to 49.6 million shares worth $2.35 billion at Sept. 30, though bitcoin’s slide since then has cut the stake’s value to about $1.82 billion.

The bank disclosed the position in a Form 13F filed Monday, covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. It reported 49,577,094 IBIT shares across five of its units, up from 24,396,222 shares worth $812.2 million in its filing for June 30. That is an increase of about 103% in share count. The reported value rose about 189%, because IBIT climbed from $33.29 to $47.34 a share during the quarter.

The fund closed at $36.79 on Monday. At that price, the same 49.6 million shares are worth roughly $1.82 billion, about $520 million less than the value in the filing.

Mostly client accounts, not a house bet

The filing does not break out how much of the position belongs to the bank and how much to its customers. But the largest single block, 32,483,714 shares worth about $1.54 billion, sits under Wells Fargo Clearing Services, the brokerage entity behind Wells Fargo Advisors. Wells Fargo Advisors Financial Network reported another 9.5 million shares, and Wells Fargo Bank reported 7.4 million.

That points to a position built largely by wealth-management clients buying the ETF in brokerage and advisory accounts, rather than a directional trade by the bank itself. A 13F lists securities over which a firm has investment discretion, which at a big bank includes managed client money.

Wells Fargo Securities, the investment-banking and trading arm, also reported IBIT options: calls on 717,200 shares and puts on 540,000 shares, valued at about $34.0 million and $25.6 million. Those figures reflect the value of the underlying shares, not the premiums paid, and they may hedge other positions. Both lines were smaller than at midyear, when the unit listed calls on 1.12 million shares and puts on 845,000.

Wells Fargo also added to its other spot bitcoin funds. Grayscale’s Bitcoin Mini Trust rose to 3.09 million shares, worth $114.1 million, from 2.56 million. Bitwise’s bitcoin ETF rose to 1.6 million shares, worth $72.6 million, from 1.38 million.

Strategy stake cut by a third

The bank moved the other way on Strategy (MSTR). Wells Fargo’s long position in the bitcoin treasury company fell to 1,339,018 shares, worth $205.0 million at Sept. 30, from 1,994,253 shares at midyear, a drop of about 33%. Wells Fargo Securities also listed Strategy puts on 795,000 shares, down from 1.52 million. Strategy closed at $103.03 on Monday, against $153.09 at the end of September.

The filing lands as big banks disclose larger bitcoin exposure through ETFs and treasury stocks. JPMorgan reported $540 million in bitcoin ETFs in its own third-quarter 13F last week. Wells Fargo’s IBIT stake is more than four times that.

The timing also stands out. Since the quarter ended, U.S. spot bitcoin funds have been losing money fast. IBIT bled about $2 billion over nine straight sessions through mid-November, and bitcoin fell to about $62,000 over the weekend before trading near $64,000 on Monday. The fund took in about $76.5 million on Monday, breaking an 11-session streak of outflows that had pulled roughly $2.35 billion from IBIT since Oct. 30. That is almost exactly the value Wells Fargo put on its own stake at the end of September.

Wells Fargo’s filing is a snapshot as of Sept. 30. It does not show whether the bank or its clients bought or sold IBIT shares in October or November, the period in which bitcoin fell from above $83,000 to the low $60,000s. The next round of 13Fs, covering the fourth quarter, is due in February.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Singapore and Germany Test Wholesale CBDC FX Settlement With Zero-Knowledge Proofs
summary:
Key Takeaways: Singapore and Germany conducted tests for cross-border EUR-SGD settlement, leveraging wholesale CBDC. No-knowledge proofs were used to settle conditions without involving the ledgers of central banks. The trial
The post Singapore and Germany Test Wholesale CBDC FX Settlement With Zero...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Singapore and Germany conducted tests for cross-border EUR-SGD settlement, leveraging wholesale CBDC.
  • No-knowledge proofs were used to settle conditions without involving the ledgers of central banks.
  • The trial was conducted by DBS, Deutsche Bank and Partior.

Singapore and Germany have finished a new digital asset settlement test, designed to link two separate central bank infrastructures. The study concentrated on the wholesale foreign exchange settlement in various currencies, systems and operating hours.

  • Project Simbolon Connects Two Central Bank Settlement Systems
  • Zero-Knowledge Proofs Help Verify Settlement Conditions
    • Wholesale CBDCs Target FX and Tokenized Asset Settlement
    • MAS and Bundesbank Plan Broader Digital Asset Testing

Project Simbolon Connects Two Central Bank Settlement Systems

The Monetary Authority of Singapore and Deutsche Bundesbank conducted a test of connectivity between their digital asset settlement test environments in Project Simbolon, marking a significant first milestone achieved under a cross-border settlement agreement they signed in November 2025.

The commercial banks involved in the experiment were DBS and Deutsche Bank, who were technology supported by Partior.

The test included euro-Singapore dollar rates and trades derogated by wholesale central bank digital currency (CBDC). The project maintains the two main banking systems independent while synchronizing settlement in both systems.

Read More: 25 BLOOM Participants Join 3 Asian Central Banks to Advance Cross-Border Digital Money

Zero-Knowledge Proofs Help Verify Settlement Conditions

Payment-for-payment (or PvP) settlement was used for Project Simbolon. Here, the transfer of one currency can be made only in conjunction with a transfer of the other currency.

Another feature of the setup: Zero-knowledge proofs. The technology enabled each settlement environment to verify that it met the required criteria without revealing any original information in the ledgers or making any technological link between the two central bank ledgers.

This architecture is especially relevant to tokenized finance since other blockchain-based or digital ledger systems could want to communicate with each other without needing to be reconstructed on top of a shared infrastructure.

Wholesale CBDCs Target FX and Tokenized Asset Settlement

Both markets are in different time zones, which means that banks might have to organise liquidity prior to the settlement. A more tightly integrated settlement model for the digital world would enable institutions to commit and source funds more in line with the time of the actual settlement.

Project Guardian, MAS’ work on institutional tokenization and more efficient tokenized financial markets greatly complements the work, said MAS. Since 2024 the Bundewanskynd has been a member of the Guardian Policymaker Group.

MAS and Bundesbank Plan Broader Digital Asset Testing

The two central banks will keep cooperating with industry on broader applications of interoperable digital asset settlement.

Further work is anticipated that will consider settlement performance, legal treatment, operating procedure, governance and regulatory considerations. Also one will be prepared to cover in greater detail the technical aspects of the architecture, testing, and potential implementation of Project Simbolon.

The crypto industry will get a further example of how central banks are exploring blockchain-related infrastructure and tokenised currency and cryptographic verification for institutional settlement, but not retail payments.

title: The Role of Cryptocurrency in Digital Entertainment
summary:
Cryptocurrency is no longer limited to assets such as Bitcoin or activities such as trading and price speculation. In recent years, cryptocurrencies and blockchain technology have been applied across several
The post The Role of Cryptocurrency in Digital Entertainment  appeared first on CryptoNinjas...
content:
Cryptocurrency is no longer limited to assets such as Bitcoin or activities such as trading and price speculation. In recent years, cryptocurrencies and blockchain technology have been applied across several industries, including digital entertainment. What’s interesting is that many people havent’actually realized that crypto has a huge impact on them.

From new payment options to digital ownership and creator rewards, digital currencies offer possibilities that traditional systems can’t always provide. But how does it all work and why should ordinary internet users care? Well, let’s find out.

  • How Cryptocurrencies Are Used Beyond Investment 
  • How Cryptocurrency Supports Digital Content Creators 
  • Blockchain and Digital Ownership in Entertainment 
  • Blockchain Applications in Online Gaming 
  • Cryptocurrency in Streaming and Online Communities 
  • The Future of Cryptocurrency in Digital Entertainment 

How Cryptocurrencies Are Used Beyond Investment 

One of the first associations people have with cryptocurrencies is Bitcoin and Ethereum. They may associate these assets with financial markets, investment opportunities and unpredictable prices, but crypto can also function as payment methods.

Instead of relying entirely on banks or traditional payment providers, users can actually transfer supported digital assets directly between eligible wallets. Some may not realize it, but this can be very useful, especially if the two people live in different parts of the world.

Cryptocurrency transfers offer an alternative to conventional payment methods, but their costs and processing times vary depending on the blockchain network, transaction fees, and the service providers involved. 

How Cryptocurrency Supports Digital Content Creators 

The creator economy is another interesting area where cryptocurrencies started playing a more important role in the last couple of years. As we all know, people like musicians, artists, streamers and even video producers usually depend on ad revenue, subscriptions and money from third-party platforms. This is where crypto comes into play because these payment options provide additional ways for creators to receive financial support from their audiences.

There have been many examples of that in the last couple of months, such as a streamer receiving crypto tips and an independent artist selling various collectibles linked to their work. All of these options can be very attractive to creators with audiences around the world. 

Blockchain and Digital Ownership in Entertainment 

The fact that people often spend a lot of money on digital products is unsurprising, as this has been the case for a long time. Video game skins, virtual accessories, downloadable content, or even exclusive online memberships are just some of the things that users are interested in. Blockchain technology introduces alternative ways to record ownership and transfer certain digital assets, although the actual rights associated with those assets depend on the platform and applicable terms. 

If you remember a few years ago, people were really interested in the so-called NFTs. They can provide a record of ownership or control over a unique digital token. There were many cases in which companies released these tokens for special content, fan experiences, or virtual items. 

Owning an NFT does not automatically grant copyright, intellectual property rights, or permanent access to the associated content. These rights depend on the issuer’s terms and the underlying platform. This distinction is important because digital ownership is way more complicated than simply holding a token in a wallet. 

Blockchain Applications in Online Gaming 

Blockchain technology and cryptocurrency have several applications in online gaming, including digital asset transactions, virtual economies, and blockchain-based gaming environments. Traditional operators only allow people to make deposits and withdrawals in fiat currencies, but modern blockchain-based games expand these options and give people far more opportunities. Some blockchain-based games also incorporate tokenized assets, digital collectibles, or decentralized marketplaces into their gameplay systems. 

Even if we look beyond different online gaming platforms, we can see that other businesses also rely heavily on cryptocurrencies. For example, there are platforms that offer token-based rewards. 

Considering the growing popularity of digital currencies and how they work, we believe it’s a matter of time before cryptocurrencies become even more popular among casual players.

Cryptocurrency in Streaming and Online Communities 

Some people may not realize it, but crypto-based technology can create additional opportunities for cryptocurrency-based tech. We believe there will be many platforms in the near future that will allow people to pay for a single movie, video or even a live event using cryptocurrencies instead of signing up for a monthly subscription. This will allow users to have more freedom to choose what they want to watch and can actually save money in the long run.

Some of the online communities could also benefit from these payment options. You can find many content creators who offer exclusive videos, special memberships, or even early access to their work. 

The Future of Cryptocurrency in Digital Entertainment 

Considering how the world is changing around us, we believe that cryptocurrencies will become even more popular than they are today. Nowadays, many people are still unfamiliar with how digital wallets work, while others are worried about fees, security, and sudden price changes.

Despite these challenges, there is a growing number of entertainment platforms that are now accepting crypto payments. These brands operate in different businesses, and they realize that using digital currencies offers them many advantages.

title: Bitrue Research Institute Releases Report Finding Growing Interest in AI-Assisted Crypto Trading
summary: San Jose, Costa RIca, 17th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

San Jose, Costa RIca, 17th November 2026, Chainwire

San Jose, Costa RIca, November 17th, 2026, Chainwire

Bitrue Research Institute report pairs the survey with open-source data showing trading agent projects grew more than fivefold in 2026

As crypto hits extreme fear, a Bitrue AI survey finds traders ready to let AI trade. Bitcoin fell to its lowest level since July over the weekend, but interest in AI-assisted trading keeps climbing: half of Bitrue users who had not yet used an AI trading bot said they are ready to try one. The findings are part of How Trading Bots Are Reshaping Web3 Trading, a new report from Bitrue Research Institute that combines a survey of Bitrue users with the institute’s analysis of public open-source development data.

The survey was sent to 8,280 Bitrue users. Half of respondents who had not yet used an AI trading bot said they are ready to try one, and 36.4% said they would like to learn a little more first. What they want most is confidence: their most common hesitation, named by 45.5%, was how losses and risk are controlled. Asked what would get them going, respondents named a clearer explanation of what the bot does, a trial reward for the first trade, and real trading examples. Users who had already tried Bitrue AI Bot most often valued the time it saves them from watching charts. The report describes the survey findings as directional.

The survey sits against a sharp rise in builder activity. Bitrue Research Institute counted new public GitHub repositories by creation year and found that projects describing themselves as “trading agents” grew from 110 in 2024 to 1,133 in 2025 and 6,121 in 2026 through Nov. 15. New projects describing crypto trading bots rose from 551 in 2024 to 2,399 in 2025.

Industry data points to the same way. In a separate industry survey of 3,708 crypto traders, 84.8% had used AI for crypto research or trading in the previous six months, and daily bot launches on one major bot platform rose 29% between July and September 2026.

The report describes five shifts behind this growth: bots moving inside exchanges, AI generating strategy setups, chat becoming a trading interface, AI agents gaining their own accounts, and trust increasingly depending on guardrails and explanation. It also profiles eight trading bots, from built-in exchange bots to multi-exchange platforms and AI copilots, highlighting what each does best rather than ranking them.

In the research, Bitrue AI is profiled as an explainable AI copilot. Each strategy shows its direction, price range, and reasoning before a user starts, with a 30-day backtest and drawdown. The market is re-scanned every 15 minutes, and users set their own take-profit, stop-loss, and maximum drawdown limits without API keys.

“Red markets are when discipline matters most, and our users are ready for AI to help,” Bitrue Research Institute said. “Half of those who have not tried an AI bot yet say they want to, and what they ask for is clarity and control. As builders move from bots to agents, the tools that explain themselves and let traders set their own limits are the ones that will bring AI trading to the mainstream.”

The report closes with practical questions for traders, covering strategy reasoning, loss limits, testing, account permissions and costs.

About Bitrue Research Institute

Bitrue Research Institute is the in-house research arm of Bitrue. It studies digital asset markets using Bitrue’s own market data alongside public market and on-chain sources, with a focus on XRP, market structure and the role of AI in trading.

About Bitrue

Founded in 2018, Bitrue is a global cryptocurrency exchange serving more than 40 million users worldwide. Bitrue was the first exchange to list XRP as a base pair and offers a broad selection of XRP trading pairs, alongside tokenized real-world assets, staking products, Launchpool offerings and Bitrue AI, its AI-powered trading copilot. PrimeXBT, a global multi-asset broker and crypto asset service provider, has announced the launch of Pre-IPO Trading, a new category within its Crypto Futures offering, starting with ANT/USDT*. The new instrument gives traders an opportunity to trade the market-implied pre-IPO valuation of Anthropic, the company behind Claude and one of the most anticipated listings of the year, before it goes public.

ANT/USDT is a USDT-margined perpetual Crypto Futures contract available on PrimeXBT’s native PXTrader 2.0 platform. Traders can open long or short positions, trade 24/7, including weekends, and use leverage of up to 1:5, with a minimum order size of 0.01 contract. title: Xsolla ZK Introduces a Gas Token Designed to Let Digital Items Move Between Games and Players
summary: Los Angeles, United States, 17th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Los Angeles, United States, 17th November 2026, Chainwire

Los Angeles, United States, November 17th, 2026, Chainwire

Xsolla ZK, Inc. is introducing Xsolla Gas (XLA), the native token of Xsolla ZK, a blockchain network for games. XLA is designed to pay the network fees that arise when players transfer or share eligible digital items on Xsolla ZK. Players who prefer not to download and set up a separate wallet can cover those fees through Xsolla Gas Station, offered by Xsolla (USA), Inc., a global commerce company, where they buy XLA-NT, a non-transferable gas credit used only to pay network fees on Xsolla ZK. Xsolla Gas Station sells only XLA-NT. Xsolla Gas pays the network fees that let players transfer the eligible in-game digital items they own.

Players want more from the games and brands they follow, and developers want ways to engage players. Digital items have become more than cosmetics; players can now collect them from their favorite games. But letting players keep, share, and give away those items can be complicated.

Most digital items today live on a single game’s backend. Players generally can’t transfer them to friends or use them in another game, and items become inaccessible if a game shuts down. Blockchain-backed items stay with the players who collect them, but transferring them requires a network fee. Players typically have to set up and manage a separate digital wallet and get the right token to pay that fee, which adds complexity.

Xsolla ZK is designed to lower these barriers. Xsolla’s existing payment, monetization, and distribution products can now use blockchain-backed items, giving developers a new way to monetize and distribute digital items and giving players new ways to keep them and give them to other players. Players use Xsolla Gas to cover the network fees required to transfer or share a digital item held in their Xsolla Backpack.

Xsolla Backpack is an inventory for the digital items a player owns. Digital items issued to the Backpack in transferable form are designed to remain available to the player even if the issuing game shuts down. A player can give them to another player. This blockchain functionality is designed to empower players to decide what happens to the eligible items they own. Digital items that remain on a game’s own backend continue to work as they do today and cannot be transferred through Backpack.

Players who want to collect these digital items sign in to their account as usual, without needing a seed phrase or a separate wallet setup. They cover network fees by buying XLA-NT gas credits through Xsolla Gas Station, using the payment methods they already know and prefer. Players can collect eligible items they purchase or claim in their Backpack and share them with other players.

“Players should be able to share and gift digital items they own, anytime, anywhere, with anyone they know,” said Chris Hewish, President of Xsolla (USA). “Developers gain a new way to monetize their games, and players gain eligible digital items that are theirs to keep. When both sides win, the games do too. We are adding options inside the tools they already use, not asking anyone to change how they work.”

When a player wants to share or give away a digital item, the transaction runs on Xsolla ZK, the blockchain network, and the network fee is paid in Xsolla Gas. This lets players hold items and give them to other players, and it is designed to let them carry items between supported games. Players can pay the fee themselves in XLA or XLA-NT. Developers and partners can also use XLA to pay network fees for their item activity.

Players can cover network fees through:

  • Xsolla Gas Station: players sign in with their Xsolla ID and buy XLA-NT gas credits through the checkout they already use. Xsolla Gas Station sells only XLA-NT, which can be used only to pay network fees.
  • Crypto exchanges: XLA is available on crypto exchanges, including Kraken, LBank, and Biconomy, in supported markets.

More than 1,500 game teams use Xsolla (USA)’s tools and services to monetize and distribute games. These tools are designed to work with Xsolla ZK to support the transfer of eligible digital items, and Xsolla Backpack and Xsolla Gas Station are now available without additional development for teams using compatible Xsolla (USA) products, integrating with existing player and payment flows. Studios, publishers, brands, and players can learn more about Xsolla Gas Station at x.la/gas.

Developers building games, wallets, marketplaces, and item services on Xsolla ZK can find network documentation, developer tools, and integration paths at xsolla.org.

Readers can also complete a short Xsolla Quest at xsolla.pro/xsolla-zk-quest to learn more about Xsolla Gas, Xsolla Gas Station, and Xsolla Backpack.

What is Xsolla Quest? Xsolla Quest lets people complete a few simple steps on an Xsolla page to receive an item.

About Xsolla

Xsolla (USA) is a global commerce company that builds and provides all the things developers need to launch, grow, and monetize video games. Headquartered in Los Angeles, California, the company supports studios of every size, from indie to AAA, with solutions across direct-to-consumer commerce, intelligent payments, entertainment-based IP, and player engagement products. Xsolla (USA) helps developers fund, distribute, market, and monetize their games at scale. Trusted by more than 70% of the top 100 highest-grossing games, Xsolla (USA) operates as the merchant of record across 200+ geographies with access to 1,000+ local payment methods worldwide. Grounded in a deep belief in the future of video games, Xsolla (USA) is resolute in bringing opportunities together and unlocking growth for creators everywhere.

For more information, visit xsolla.com.

About Xsolla ZK

Xsolla ZK is an Ethereum Layer 2 network for games, built as a ZK rollup. Its gas token, XLA, is an ERC-20 token on Ethereum mainnet with a total supply of 1 billion. XLA becomes the base token of Xsolla ZK through the canonical bridge. Every transaction on the network, including claiming a game item, pays gas in XLA. Users can pay in XLA-NT, a non-transferable gas credit used only to pay network fees on Xsolla ZK.

For more information on Xsolla ZK, visit xsolla.org

Xsolla Gas Station and XLA-NT are offered by Xsolla (USA), Inc. Xsolla Gas Station sells only XLA-NT. XLA-NT is a non-transferable credit that can be used only to pay network fees on Xsolla ZK. It cannot be transferred or sold and cannot be redeemed for cash or other crypto. XLA and XLA-NT are designed for paying network fees and are not offered as investments. Crypto prices can change quickly. Xsolla (USA)’s Web3 products are not offered to, and may not be used by, any person or entity that is: (a) located or resident in any country, territory, or U.S. state where Xsolla (USA) restricts access; (b) subject to applicable sanctions, or owned or controlled by a sanctioned party; or (c) otherwise barred by local law from using them.

title: Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders, Raising Crypto Phishing Risks
summary:
Key Takeaways: Data on approximately 27,000 orders was revealed after a breach of Trezor’s shipping partner, Skladon. The affected records included names, addresses, phone numbers and purchase information, among other
The post Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders, Raising Crypto Phis...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Data on approximately 27,000 orders was revealed after a breach of Trezor’s shipping partner, Skladon.
  • The affected records included names, addresses, phone numbers and purchase information, among other things.
  • Trezor states that they are safe at this time, but the risk of phishing becomes greater to the customer.

Trezor has warned customers about a data breach at logistics partner Skladon that exposed personal information linked to roughly 27,000 hardware wallet orders. The incident introduces a new phishing and physical security risk since the bad guys can now know both the buyer of a crypto wallet and its delivery address.

  • Skladon Breach Exposes Hardware Wallet Order Data
    • Real Order Details Could Make Phishing More Convincing
  • Trezor Expands Anonymous Pickup After the Breach
    • Trezor Reviews Third-Party Security Controls

Skladon Breach Exposes Hardware Wallet Order Data

Skladon reported on Nov. 15 to Trezor that the attackers had accessed the company’s systems with unauthorized access for customer shipping information. The leak happened on Nov. 7, Trezor said. The leaky data is from orders from Aug. 9 to Nov. 7, 2026.

These details were exposed: entire names, telephones, e-mail addresses, delivery addresses and order information including purchased products. Trezor suspects the source of the attacking data has been exported, and as far as it can determine, it is still ongoing.

Trezor emphasized that it was not the infrastructure of theirs being hacked. The leak didn’t include wallet backups, PINs & passphrases, and neither Trezor nor Skladon saves PINs and passphrases.

Read More: Coinone Customer Data Breach Sparks Fresh Phishing Risk for South Korean Crypto Users

Real Order Details Could Make Phishing More Convincing

The greatest danger now is scams created from the real customer data.

Some users have already reported receiving calls they deemed to be scams due to the event, Trezor said. If an attacker provides a name, hardware wallet type, hardware wallet price or other delivery data, email, text or a physical letter would seem genuine.

The company warned anyone else who was using Trezor to watch out for this kind of operation, stating that it will never cold-call nor ask for their wallet backup. Support services should be called directly from the Trezor website, not via links, QR codes or numbers provided in spam messages.

Home addresses were leaked as well, and that’s why Trezor noted there were potential physical security issues if the customer that bought it revealed that they were a crypto owner.

Trezor Expands Anonymous Pickup After the Breach

Currently, Trezor is cutting down on personally identifiable data needed for shipping of the hardware wallets.

For its Anonymous Pickup service, it operates in 18 European countries and lets its clients collect items from lockers and/or collect points without sharing their real name, home address, or telephone number with Trezor.

The firm is also reducing the amount of time it retains order data, now from 90 to 45 days and will further slice that down. Shipping partners will be required to have the same retention policy.

Trezor Reviews Third-Party Security Controls

The Skladon incident comes on the heels of another 2026 incident that occurred with a different Trezor fulfillment partner, ShipMonk, that impacted over 80,000 users. Trezor has stated it is looking at its ties with third party logistics providers and the measures used to appoint them.

The incident demonstrates that while self-custody safeguards private keys, it doesn’t remove potential risks associated with the manufacturing and delivery of physical crypto wallets.

content:
2026-11-17T14:24:00.000+02:00

Tuesday, 17/11/2026 | 12:24 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Balances reached $470.50 million in September, 1.77% above June, though the month added only 0.12%.
  • OANDA regained $3.03 million as Gain Capital lost $3.12 million, and crypto apps' futures arms added $56 million.

Client money at US retail forex dealers grew in the third quarter, after three straight quarterly declines. The six registered dealers owed retail customers $470.50 million at the end of September, according to Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) data.

That total is 1.77% above June's $462.31 million, a figure FinanceMagnates.com reported in August as the lowest since at least September 2023.

The recovery is small against a market of six firms. Balances remain 6.95% below the $505.62 million held a year earlier, although the annual gap narrowed from 7.23% in August, and September itself added only $540,751, or 0.12%.

London's trading industry is coming home!

OANDA and Gain Capital Move in Opposite Directions

Under the flat total, the two largest dealers moved by almost the same amount in opposite directions.

OANDA added $3.03 million, or 2.31% from August, to reach $134.41 million. It was the first monthly increase since May, after an August balance of $131.38 million that FinanceMagnates.com described as the lowest since at least September 2023.

Gain Capital, the StoneX subsidiary behind FOREX.com, lost $3.12 million, or 1.53% on the month, and ended at $201.04 million. The two dealers still hold 71.30% of all US retail forex balances, almost unchanged from August.

OANDA's owner FTMO plans to hire about 300 people over 14 months, roughly half of them for teams at the broker.

The other four dealers split evenly. On the same monthly measure, tastyfx, IG Group's US brand, rose 1.65% to $49.90 million and Interactive Brokers gained 1.74% to $27.05 million, while Charles Schwab Futures and Forex slipped 0.51% to $55.61 million.

Trading.com posted the steepest monthly fall, down 12.63% to $2.49 million. Taken together, the three dealers that grew added $4.31 million and the three that shrank lost $3.77 million.

Annual Gap Widest at Interactive Brokers

Over twelve months, tastyfx is the outlier. Its balance is 14.08% above September 2025, the largest annual gain among the six, while Trading.com is up 1.20%.

Interactive Brokers sits at the other end, 20.87% below a year earlier, even as its wider business grew. The broker reported $964.7 billion in client equity for September, up 27% year over year.

OANDA is down 8.74%, Charles Schwab Futures and Forex 7.78% and Gain Capital 7.63%. Trading activity across the retail industry also rose in the quarter: preliminary data put retail trading volumes up an estimated 8% quarter on quarter in Q3 2026, FM Intelligence's broker volumes tracker shows.

Crypto Apps' Futures Brokers Pull Further Ahead

The futures brokers owned by Coinbase and Robinhood grew much faster in September. Their segregated client money rose $55.97 million, or 9.63% from August, to $637.32 million, more than 100 times the forex industry's monthly gain.

In August the two held $581.4 million, more than the six forex dealers combined, according to an FM Intelligence analysis of the same CFTC filings. By September their balance was 1.35 times the forex total, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation.

Coinbase Financial Markets accounted for most of the increase, adding $41.97 million, or 12.10%, while Robinhood Derivatives added $14.00 million to $248.45 million.

The regulator's October 5 notice on a retail crypto framework contemplates leveraged retail crypto purchases only through futures commission merchants or banks they sponsor.

The two measures differ. Futures balances cover every futures client at those firms, and the forex figure is what dealers owe retail forex clients at month end, adjusted for trading profit and loss.

Coinbase Financial Markets ended September with $388.86 million, more than the $335.45 million that OANDA and Gain Capital owed their retail forex clients combined.

title: Tether Bets $15M on Nomad to Push USDT and XAUT Deeper Into Brazil’s Crypto Market

The post Tether Bets $15M on Nomad to Push USDT and XAUT Deeper Into Brazil’s Crypto Market appeared fi...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Tether Capital has poured $15 million into Brazilian fintech company Nomad.
  • The companies could consider integrations between USDT and Tether Gold.
  • Brazil continues to be one of the most stable markets for stablecoin activity.

Tether has now expanded its presence in Brazil by investing in the fintech firm Nomad, which enables its Brazilian users to have a U.S. dollar account, and make cross-border payments and global investments. This transaction might provide a new distribution avenue for USDT and XAUT issued based on gold.

  • Tether Targets Brazil’s Demand for Digital Dollars
  • Stablecoins Already Dominate Brazil’s Crypto Market
    • USDT and XAUT Could Expand Nomad’s Crypto Offering
    • Tether Builds More Links Between Crypto and Payments

Tether Targets Brazil’s Demand for Digital Dollars

The investment was made by Tether Capital on Nov. 16, noting that the partnership may enable Tether’s digital asset system to be brought into Nomad’s financial system.

The companies have intentions to conduct potential integration work with USDT and Tether Gold (XAUT). Tether has not released a date for its launches nor confirmed the existence of any of the two tokens on the Nomad network yet.

That distinction is important. Instead of providing a ready-to-use crypto service, this investment opens the way for future stablecoin products. Yet If the integrations occur, Tether will have a significant customer base with more than 3.8 million customers already using Nomad.

Read More: Tether Opens Global AI and Product Jobs to Advance Its Decentralized Tech Vision

Stablecoins Already Dominate Brazil’s Crypto Market

Brazil proved to be a great opportunity for expansion of Tether. About 80% of the volume reported for crypto trading in 2025 was in stablecoins, per data from the Federal Revenue Service of Brazil. From August 2019 to December 2025 USDT represented 88.7% of the amount traded in stablecoins (about R$1 trillion).

The amount of use indicates that stablecoins are already beginning to be used for more than speculation in Brazil. The rise of dollar-linked digital assets is a part of the country’s increased need for foreign-currency exposure and financial access across the globe.

USDT and XAUT Could Expand Nomad’s Crypto Offering

Nomad is not a crypto platform per se but rather mainstream financial services providers based on traditional dollars.

A projected USDT integration could provide another avenue of dollar exposure for users, and XAUT could enable some exposure to gold tokens. The latter are international payments, saving and investment products are part of the spaces where the companies could explore, Tether said.

The collaboration aligns with Tether Capital’s overall investment approach of focusing on companies that bridge traditional finance and digital assets.

Read More: Tether Q3 Profit Hits $1.5B While USDT Reserve Buffer Nearly Doubles to $8B

Tether Builds More Links Between Crypto and Payments

Over the past few years, Tether has increasingly seized opportunities to extend USDT beyond crypto exchanges to payments and financial infrastructure and consumer services.

For the CEO, Paolo Ardoino, the investment into the Nomad is indicative of Tether’s strategy to offer its products via financial platforms that users are familiar with.

The deal could make stablecoins a more regular part of the day-to-day cross-border payments for Brazil. In the eyes of the Bitcoin token Tether, it offers a direct path to a market already extremely in demand for digital dollars.

title: JPMorgan and DBS Take Dollar Transfers Into the Weekend—With One Important Catch
summary: JPMorgan and DBS have connected their tokenized deposit networks for round-the-clock dollar transfers. The launch shows banks putting blockchain to work, while a Saturday maintenance window reveals where the older system still matters.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: JPM

JPMorgan and DBS have connected their tokenized deposit networks for round-the-clock dollar transfers. The launch shows banks putting blockchain to work, while a Saturday maintenance window reveals where the older system still matters.

JPMorgan and DBS have connected their blockchain deposit networks so institutional clients can move tokenized U.S. dollars between Singapore and the United States around the clock, including weekends.

The November 16 launch announcement names Ant International as the first client. It is a concrete move from planning to commercial availability for a form of digital money that keeps banks at the centre of the transaction.

The appeal is straightforward: businesses operate across time zones even when conventional banking processes pause. But the service also exposes a boundary in the always-on promise—moving money between JPMorgan’s legacy deposit accounts and blockchain accounts still has a Saturday interruption.

What JPMorgan and DBS have actually launched

The link joins DBS Token Services with Kinexys by J.P. Morgan’s account-based permissioned deposit network. Partior coordinates settlement. The stated use case is institutional dollar liquidity between accounts in the two markets.

Rachel Chew, DBS’s chief operating officer and co-head of digital assets for global transaction services, said tokenized money was moving towards “delivering live tangible value for clients.”

The announcement’s footnote qualifies the operating hours. Transfers within the Kinexys blockchain account network run continuously, but moving funds between those accounts and traditional demand deposit accounts pauses from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern Time each Saturday. DBS says an enhancement is being developed.

Why the account boundary matters

For a treasury team, money already inside the relevant network and money still sitting in a conventional account are different operational starting points. An available transfer route is useful only if the funds can reach it when needed.

Consider a hypothetical business that expects a weekend funding requirement. Keeping suitable liquidity in the supported account beforehand could make the new connection valuable. Leaving everything outside it until the maintenance window would raise a different question.

That does not negate the service’s usefulness. It shows why companies need to assess the whole payment journey: funding, transfer, receipt and the recipient’s ability to use the balance. Speed in one stage cannot answer every question about the others.

Likewise, a transfer completing across this link does not establish that every unrelated supplier can receive an immediate conventional bank payment. Eligibility, account access and onward payment arrangements remain relevant.

A year-old framework becomes a working connection

The banks’ November 2025 framework announcement described plans to connect their separate on-chain ecosystems. At the time, each already offered round-the-clock capabilities within its own environment.

The proposed next step was exchangeability and settlement across the two systems, with ambitions spanning public and permissioned blockchains. The newly announced service should be judged on its specified permissioned-account connection, rather than assuming every part of that broader ambition is now available.

This is the interoperability problem in practical terms. A fast network inside one bank has limited reach if customers cannot readily transact with another bank’s network. Connecting institutions can be more useful than making an already quick internal transfer slightly faster.

Tokenized deposits keep the bank in the picture

DBS describes Token Services as a suite of blockchain banking capabilities covering programmable value transfers, liquidity management and payment controls. Its proposition is an extension of banking services using tokenization and smart contracts.

A tokenized bank deposit remains a claim associated with a bank account. It differs from simply acquiring a freely circulating cryptocurrency for a personal wallet. The relevant questions include which institution owes the money, who may participate and how transfers are governed.

For stablecoin issuers, that creates competition over a particular job: moving digital dollar value when customers need it. It does not mean one launch replaces the many uses of public-chain stablecoins or creates demand for every blockchain token.

The commercial contest will turn partly on reach. A corporate service can be attractive within an approved banking relationship while serving a different customer from someone seeking an open wallet-to-wallet payment.

For an institution choosing between these routes, the useful comparison is total cost, availability and operational fit. A familiar bank relationship could matter as much as the underlying ledger technology.

Singapore’s wider plan includes AI payments

The Monetary Authority of Singapore’s Project BLOOM sets out a wider effort to improve domestic and cross-border settlement. It includes regulated stablecoins and tokenized commercial-bank money, alongside interoperability and programmable controls.

Its focus areas also include payments by AI agents within predefined limits and safeguards. That is a policy and development direction, not a claim that the new DBS–JPMorgan link has already enabled autonomous consumer spending.

BNC’s report on AI agents paying for computing with Bitcoin examined another route towards automated transactions. Together, the developments show why payment infrastructure matters to AI as well as finance: software needs both authority to spend and a way to settle.

The next test for the banks is sustained customer usage, broader connectivity and fewer interruptions at the boundaries. The launch provides a specific new dollar route. Its significance will grow if companies can use it reliably as part of everyday cash management.

summary: Bitcoin's valuation metrics are flashing a possible bottom signal, but persistent ETF withdrawals and weak on-chain demand continue to complicate the outlook for BTC, ETH, and XRP.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC ETH XRP

Bitcoin's valuation metrics are flashing a possible bottom signal, but persistent ETF withdrawals and weak on-chain demand continue to complicate the outlook for BTC, ETH, and XRP.

Bitcoin (BTC) traded at $64,946.14 after recovering from an early session low near $64,357. Ethereum (ETH) and XRP each gained 1.04%, reaching $1,838.34 and $0.9646, respectively. The rebound follows a sharp market correction that pushed Bitcoin toward $62,000 over the weekend.

The latest developments have placed Bitcoin’s MVRV ratio, short-term holder cost basis, and institutional investment flows at the center of market discussions. While some on-chain indicators suggest BTC is approaching historically undervalued territory, declining apparent demand raises questions about whether buyers can sustain a recovery. Current asset prices and broader market movements can be tracked through Brave New Coin’s Bitcoin price chart and cryptocurrency market dashboard.

Bitcoin MVRV Near 1.1 Revives Historical Market Bottom Signals

CryptoQuant’s latest analysis shows Bitcoin’s Market Value to Realized Value (MVRV) ratio falling below 1.2, with its current reading hovering around 1.1. The indicator compares Bitcoin’s market capitalization with its realized capitalization, which estimates the value of circulating coins based on the prices at which they last moved on-chain.

Bitcoin’s MVRV ratio near 1.1 at $64,100 mirrors the undervaluation levels seen around the 2022 market bottom before a significant recovery. Source: CryptoQuant via X

A declining MVRV ratio generally indicates that the market’s aggregate valuation is approaching the average cost basis of its holders. Historically, readings below 1.2 have appeared during periods of substantial market stress, when unrealized profits across the network have contracted, and Bitcoin has approached potential accumulation zones.

CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost highlighted this historical relationship, describing the sub-1.2 reading as a signal of “a forming market bottom.” The analyst also noted that the indicator had reached similar levels during the 2022 bear market, when Bitcoin traded between approximately $16,000 and $21,000 before beginning its subsequent recovery.

The current reading represents the third time the signal has appeared during the 2026 bear market. Previous occurrences emerged in February, when BTC approached $60,000, and again during June and July, when the cryptocurrency declined toward $57,000.

However, historical similarities do not establish that another bottom has already formed. MVRV measures market valuation relative to on-chain cost basis, rather than identifying fresh buying activity. A low reading can therefore persist while prices remain under pressure, particularly when investors continue reducing their exposure.

Bitcoin Tests Short-Term Holder Cost Basis Cluster

Glassnode’s latest cost-basis distribution analysis provides another important reference for Bitcoin’s current price structure. Its November 11 report identified a concentrated short-term holder supply band between $62,000 and $66,000, associated with coins acquired around the August market low.

Bitcoin is trading near its densest short-term holder cost-basis cluster, with concentrated supply between $63,000 and $65,000. Source: Glassnode via X

Glassnode described the distribution by stating that “the only dense block sits between $62K and $66K.” With Bitcoin trading near $65,000, its price has returned to this concentrated acquisition zone. The area could influence near-term trading as investors who purchased during that period reassess their positions.

The broader short-term holder picture remains less encouraging. Glassnode placed the average short-term holder cost basis at approximately $75,600, representing the average acquisition price for investors who purchased or last moved their Bitcoin within the previous 155 days. Its November 11 assessment found that only about 35% of short-term holder coins remained profitable.

This creates two separate market considerations. The $62,000–$66,000 distribution band identifies a concentrated area of recent acquisition activity, while the higher $75,600 average cost basis indicates that much of the broader short-term holder cohort remains underwater.

If Bitcoin maintains its position around the lower cluster, the area could provide a reference for near-term stabilization. However, a sustained decline below it would place more recent buyers into unrealized losses and could increase selling pressure if holders decide to exit their positions.

Bitcoin Apparent Demand Remains Deeply Negative

Despite the encouraging MVRV reading, Bitcoin’s demand indicators continue to present a significant concern. CryptoQuant analyst MorenoDV reported that BTC’s 30-day apparent demand stood near negative 247,700 BTC on November 15, while the one-year reading reached approximately negative 1.21 million BTC.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Apparent demand estimates the difference between newly issued Bitcoin and changes in the supply of coins that have remained inactive for more than a year. It helps assess whether new issuance is being absorbed by market participants or whether older supply is returning to circulation faster than new coins are being issued.

The persistent negative readings indicate that the market has not established a sustained accumulation trend. CryptoQuant also observed that demand failed to recover meaningfully during previous Bitcoin rebounds toward $80,000–$85,000, suggesting that those advances lacked confirmation from this on-chain indicator.

The analyst identified “the repeated failure of demand to recover” as the central concern. This distinction is important because a deeply negative apparent demand reading does not directly measure capital leaving the market or establish how many Bitcoins have been sold. Instead, it provides an estimate of changes in supply dynamics based on issuance and coin activity.

For a more convincing recovery, the 30-day reading would need to improve consistently and eventually return above zero. Stabilization in the annual measure would provide additional evidence that broader demand conditions are changing.

ETF Outflows Continue to Weigh on Bitcoin and Ethereum

Institutional investment flows provide another indication of the market’s current weakness. According to The Block’s November 14 reporting, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $1.07 billion in net outflows during the week ending November 13.

The withdrawals marked the second consecutive week in which Bitcoin investment funds lost more than $1 billion. Over seven consecutive trading sessions, the funds recorded approximately $1.91 billion in net outflows, highlighting continued institutional caution during the latest price correction.

Ethereum (ETH) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Ethereum investment products experienced similar pressure. Spot ETH ETFs recorded approximately $398.9 million in weekly withdrawals, marking their seventh consecutive week of net outflows. The prolonged withdrawal period has weighed on Ethereum’s medium-term outlook despite its recent intraday recovery.

These figures suggest that the latest market bounce has not yet been accompanied by a meaningful reversal in institutional investment flows. A stabilization in ETF demand could help improve market conditions, although fund movements alone cannot determine the direction of future prices.

ETH and XRP Join the Intraday Crypto Market Recovery

Ethereum has shown some short-term strength alongside Bitcoin’s modest recovery. ETH climbed 1.04% to $1,838.34 after touching an intraday low near $1,809. The move also pushed the asset above immediate resistance around $1,827, suggesting that buyers are attempting to regain short-term control.

Oversold conditions have encouraged some buying activity following the recent decline. However, seven consecutive weeks of negative net flows from spot Ethereum ETFs remain a concern. The recovery therefore represents an improvement in intraday momentum rather than confirmation of a broader trend reversal.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Brave New Coin’s recent Ethereum price analysis also examines the $1,700 support region and the resistance levels ETH needs to reclaim to improve its technical structure.

XRP has followed a similar pattern, rising 1.04% to $0.9646 after recovering from an early session low near $0.9510. The rebound has brought the token closer to the psychologically important $1.00 level, although its broader technical structure remains bearish.

XRP continues to trade below its key moving averages, indicating that sellers retain control of the prevailing trend. Traders are watching the $0.895 support area, which could become important if another round of selling emerges. A sustained recovery above $1.00 would provide an initial indication of improving momentum, but further confirmation would be necessary to reverse the broader decline.

What Could Confirm a Bitcoin Market Bottom?

Bitcoin’s latest on-chain readings present a mixed picture. The MVRV ratio near 1.1 suggests that aggregate market valuation has moved into territory historically associated with bear-market bottoms. Glassnode’s cost-basis distribution also identifies a concentrated supply region around current prices.

However, negative apparent demand and continued ETF withdrawals show that market participation remains weak. The divergence between lower valuations and limited accumulation makes it difficult to establish whether Bitcoin has entered a durable recovery phase.

A sustained improvement in demand, a reduction in institutional withdrawals, and stronger price action around the $62,000–$66,000 region would provide additional evidence of stabilization. Reclaiming higher cost-basis levels would also help improve the position of recent investors.

For ETH and XRP, the immediate challenge remains maintaining their intraday gains and overcoming nearby resistance. Ethereum needs to build on its move above $1,827, while XRP must regain the $1.00 level and improve its position relative to key moving averages.

For now, the latest rebound offers some relief after a difficult trading period, but the underlying data remain mixed. Bitcoin’s MVRV reading raises the possibility of a developing market bottom, while weak demand and ETF withdrawals indicate that a sustained recovery has yet to receive broader confirmation.

What is Hyperliquid? A Comprehensive Look to The Crypto Platform

Hyperliquid is a decentralized exchange built on its own layer 1 blockchain. The crypto trading platform combines the best features of centralized and decentralized exchanges to offer users fast transactions, low trading fees, advanced trading features, and a smooth interface, all without an intermediary, as in centralized exchanges.

The Hyperliquid platform specializes in perpetual futures trading, allowing users to trade crypto derivatives without owning the underlying assets. For developers, Hyperliquid is an Ethereum-compatible smart contract platform (HyperEVM), which enables them to build DeFi applications within its ecosystem.

Additionally, the Hyperliquid protocol has a native cryptocurrency, HYPE. The HYPE token serves as the backbone of the Hyperliquid ecosystem. It plays a key role in governance, staking, and enabling advanced transactions within the HyperEVM.

About Hyperliquid Crypto Project and Team

Hyperliquid is a DEX designed to combine the speed and user experience of CEXs with the transparency and security of DeFi. The project was co-founded by Jeff Yan and Iliensinc, both Harvard alumni with strong backgrounds in finance and blockchain technology. Jeff Yan has expertise in quantitative trading, while Iliensinc, though pseudonymous, is highly respected for his skills in blockchain infrastructure.

The team also includes members from prestigious institutions, such as Caltech and MIT, as well as professionals from top firms like Citadel and Hudson River Trading. The project prioritizes community, which is reflected in their rejection of venture capital funding, allocating 70% of its tokens to users, and the redistribution of all revenue back to the community.

Key Features of Hyperliquid Crypto Exchange

The key features of Hyperliquid crypto exchange are an on-chain order book, gas-free transactions, high leverage trading, liquidity vaults, cross-chain compatibility, and pro-level trading tools.

On-Chain Order Book

Most decentralized exchanges use off-chain order books or automated market makers due to the high throughput required by on-chain order books. However, the platform runs its order book on-chain, providing transparency, security, and speed-optimized transactions through its custom consensus mechanism, HyperBFT, which can confirm up to 200,000 transactions per second using Byzantine Fault Tolerance.

Gas-Free Transactions

Since Hyperliquid operates on its own Layer 1 chain, it controls the entire infrastructure and does not require users to pay gas fees for transactions, unlike Ethereum or other public blockchains. Instead, the platform covers the underlying transaction costs internally and charges users only minimal fees.

High Leverage Trading

Hyperliquid offers up to 40x leverage on perpetual futures contracts, allowing traders to amplify their positions beyond what their actual trading capital can carry. Due to the high risk associated with leverage trading, this feature is particularly tailored to experienced traders who are familiar with the strategy and want to increase their profit potential from rapid market movements.

Liquidity Vaults

Liquidity vaults on Hyperliquid are created by individuals or entities who want to share their trading strategies with others. Users can deposit funds into these vaults and earn a share of the profits or losses based on the vault leader’s trading performance. Aside from user-owned vaults, the Hyperliquid platform features protocol vaults, such as the Hyperliquidity Provider (HLP) Vault, which acts as a market maker and liquidation mechanism, earning a portion of the trading fees.

Cross-Chain Compatibility

Previously, users had to bridge into Arbitrum before accessing Hyperliquid. With the recent Router Nitro Integration, Hyperliquid now supports single‑step deposits from over 30 blockchains, including major EVM chains (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Polygon, etc.) and non‑EVM networks like Solana, Sui, Tron. This integration eliminates the previous process that required traders to bridge funds through Arbitrum before accessing Hyperliquid.

Pro-level Trading Tools

Another standout feature of Hyperliquid is the advanced trading tools available to traders, which are similar to those used by professional traders on traditional exchanges. This includes features such as the on-chain order book, real-time charts, customizable order types (including limit, market, and stop orders), in-depth market data, and responsive user interfaces, catering to both retail and institutional traders.

What Are the Pros and Cons of Hyperliquid?

The pros of Hyperliquid are listed below:

  • Advanced Trading Features: Hyperliquid offers a wide range of trading options, including spot trading, perpetual trading, pre-launch futures contracts, margin trading, and up to 40x leverage. Additionally, it supports multiple order types, including market, limit, stop market, stop limit, scale, and TWAP orders, providing traders with advanced tools to execute various strategies.
  • Community-Owned Liquidity Pools (Vaults): The Hyperliquid platform features an advanced vault system, where users can open their own vaults or contribute deposits to existing ones, sharing in the profits (about 10%).
  • Fast Transactions on a Custom Layer 1 Blockchain: Hyperliquid operates on its own Layer 1 blockchain, utilizing a proprietary HyperBFT proof-of-stake consensus that enables up to 200,000 transactions per second, with near-instant finality and very low latency.
  • Low Fees and No Gas Charges on Trades: Thanks to its PoS consensus and efficient design, Hyperliquid charges very low maker (0.045%) and taker (0.015%) fees and eliminates gas fees for trading transactions, significantly reducing trading costs compared to most other decentralized exchanges.
  • Broad Asset Support and Cross-Chain Bridging: The platform supports over 100 assets, including major cryptocurrencies like BTC, ETH, AVAX, SOL, and SUI. It also offers multiple bridges (Arbitrum Bridge, Synapse, HyBridge) to facilitate cross-chain transfers, enhancing liquidity and user flexibility.
  • User-Friendly Experience with One-Click Trading: The Hyperliquid decentralized perpetual exchange simplifies trading with one-click order execution and wallet connection. This helps to avoid repeated confirmations and streamlines the trading experience, similar to centralized platforms.
  • Governance and Community Focus: The native HYPE token enables governance participation and incentivizes trading activity. The platform is community-oriented, rejecting venture capital funding and reinvesting profits in users, which solidifies a more user-focused ecosystem.

The cons of Hyperliquid are listed below:

  • Limited Withdrawal Options: Currently, USDC is the primary cryptocurrency supported for withdrawals. If you wish to withdraw another cryptocurrency or stablecoin from Hyperliquid, you will first need to convert it to USDC. 
  • Centralization: Although Hyperliquid claims to be fully decentralized, some have criticized Hyperliquid for its relatively centralized structure. Critics argue that the protocol is not truly decentralized in comparison to other Layer-1 blockchain networks like Ethereum. 
  • Systemic Risk and Operational Concerns: The platform has faced criticism over incidents such as the JELLY token controversy, where a large trader’s actions resulted in substantial losses for liquidity providers. Critics argue that mixed vaults expose users to systemic risk and that unrestricted position sizes allow potential manipulation.

Hyperliquid is accessible in major global markets, including the United Kingdom, Singapore, South Africa, Hong Kong, France, Nigeria, Australia, Vietnam, and many others, spanning over 180 countries. Users in these supported countries can trade over 100 crypto assets on the platform without requiring Know Your Customer (KYC) verification.

These restrictions apply regardless of citizenship or physical presence, meaning individuals or entities residing, incorporated, or operating in these regions are barred from accessing Hyperliquid’s platform interface.

To create a new Hyperliquid account to buy crypto, visit Hyperliquid’s official website, then connect your wallet. You can choose to either use an email wallet or import an already existing EVM-compatible wallet. Below is a step-by-step guide for both methods.
